If unmitigated, such FOCI would pose risks to the integrity and protection of classified national defense information, the continuity of critical defense supply chains, the safeguarding of export-controlled technologies subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations and the Export Administration Regulations, and the broader national security interests of the United States.**

**Covered Transaction.** The Committee has determined that the proposed acquisition constitutes a \"covered transaction\" within the meaning of 31 C.F.R. § 800.213, and that Meridian, as a \"foreign person\" within the meaning of 31 C.F.R. § 800.224, would acquire \"control\" within the meaning of 31 C.F.R. § 800.208 over a U.S. business that is engaged in activities that are critical to the national security of the United States.

**Filing History.** The parties filed a joint voluntary notice with CFIUS on January 15, 2025. The Committee initiated its forty-five (45) day review period under 50 U.S.C. § 4565(b)(1)(E) on January 22, 2025. The Committee subsequently commenced an investigation under 50 U.S.C. § 4565(b)(2) on March 7, 2025, upon determining that the transaction is a covered transaction that may impair the national security of the United States and that cannot be resolved through the review process alone.

**CFIUS Monitoring Contact.** The designated CFIUS monitoring contact for this transaction is Dr. Samuel Keene, Director of Investment Security, Office of Investment Security, U.S. Department of the Treasury.

**[IV. DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in these National Security Terms and as incorporated into the Mitigation Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in 31 C.F.R. Part 800 or, if not defined therein, their ordinary and customary meanings.

**\"Classified Information\"** means any information that has been determined pursuant to Executive Order 13526 (or any successor executive order) to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and that is marked to indicate its classified status when in documentary form, including information classified at the CONFIDENTIAL, SECRET, TOP SECRET, and TOP SECRET/SCI levels, and including all national security information as defined in Executive Order 13526.

**\"Classified Spaces\" means any physical area within a Saxonbrook facility that is accredited by the cognizant security agency for the storage, processing, discussion, or handling of Classified Information, including all Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) and any other areas approved for classified work under the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM, 32 C.F.R. Part 117).**

**\"Closing\" or \"Closing Date\" means the date on which the stock purchase transaction described in Section II is consummated and Meridian acquires legal title to the shares of Saxonbrook common stock being purchased.**

**\"Committee\"** or **\"CFIUS\"** means the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States, as established and constituted pursuant to Section 721 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, including the Staff Chairperson and the staff of the Committee.

**\"DCSA\"** means the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency, the cognizant security agency responsible for administration of the National Industrial Security Program.

**\"Export-Controlled Technical Data\"** means any technical data, technology, defense articles, defense services, software, or other information that is controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 C.F.R. Parts 120--130, or the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), 15 C.F.R. Parts 730--774, regardless of whether such information is also classified. For the avoidance of doubt, Export-Controlled Technical Data is a broader category than Classified Information and encompasses unclassified information that is subject to export control restrictions under the ITAR or EAR.

**\"Foreign Acquirer\"** means Meridian Aerospace Holdings Ltd., together with its successors and assigns.

**\"Foreign National\"** means any individual who is not a United States citizen or United States national, and any entity that is not organized under the laws of the United States or a state or territory thereof, or that is otherwise a \"foreign person\" within the meaning of 31 C.F.R. § 800.224.

**\"Government Security Director\"** or **\"GSD\"** means the individual appointed pursuant to Requirement 2 of Section V herein.

**\"Mitigation Agreement\"** means the binding agreement to be negotiated and executed by the parties in accordance with these NST, incorporating all of the requirements set forth in Section V herein.

**\"Parties\" means Saxonbrook, Meridian, and any other entity that becomes a signatory to the Mitigation Agreement.**

**\"Security Committee\" means a committee of the board of directors of Saxonbrook composed exclusively of CFIUS-approved independent U.S. citizen directors, as described in Requirement 1 of Section V herein.**

**\"Staff Chairperson\"** means the Staff Chairperson of CFIUS, as designated by the Secretary of the Treasury pursuant to Executive Order 11858, as amended.

**\"Third-Party Monitor\"** means the independent third-party compliance monitor appointed pursuant to Requirement 8 of Section V herein.

**\"U.S. Business\" means Saxonbrook Precision Systems, Inc., together with its subsidiaries and controlled affiliates.**

**\"Voting Trust\"** or **\"Proxy Agreement\"** means the arrangement described in Requirement 3 of Section V herein, together referred to as the \"Voting Arrangement.\"

**\"Voting Trustee\"** means the independent trustee or proxy holder appointed to administer the Voting Arrangement in accordance with Requirement 3 of Section V herein.

**[V. NATIONAL SECURITY REQUIREMENTS]{.underline}**

The Mitigation Agreement shall incorporate, at a minimum, each of the following requirements. The parties may include additional provisions that exceed but do not conflict with or diminish these requirements. Each requirement is mandatory and must be reflected in the final Mitigation Agreement in a manner satisfactory to CFIUS. In the event of any ambiguity or conflict between the Mitigation Agreement and these NST, the terms of these NST shall control.

**Requirement 1 --- Board Composition**

1.1. The board of directors of Saxonbrook (the \"Board\") shall, at all times following the Closing Date, include a minimum of three (3) independent directors who are United States citizens and who have been approved by CFIUS in advance of their appointment (the \"CFIUS-Approved Directors\").

1.2. The CFIUS-Approved Directors shall comprise a majority of the Board at all times. This requirement shall be maintained irrespective of the total number of directors serving on the Board at any given time. For the avoidance of doubt, if the Board consists of seven (7) members, a minimum of four (4) must be CFIUS-Approved Directors; if the Board consists of five (5) members, a minimum of three (3) must be CFIUS-Approved Directors; and so on for any other total board size.

1.3. Each CFIUS-Approved Director must satisfy all of the following criteria:

> \(a\) be a citizen of the United States;
>
> \(b\) hold, or be eligible to obtain and hold, a personnel security clearance at the TOP SECRET/SCI level;
>
> \(c\) have no current employment, consulting, advisory, or financial relationship with Meridian or any affiliate, subsidiary, parent, or related entity of Meridian, and shall not have held any such relationship within the prior three (3) years; and
>
> \(d\) be approved in writing by CFIUS prior to appointment to the Board.

1.4. The Board shall establish a Security Committee composed exclusively of CFIUS-Approved Directors, which shall have sole and exclusive authority over all matters relating to classified contracts, facility security, personnel security, export control compliance, and compliance with the Mitigation Agreement. The Security Committee shall meet no less than quarterly and shall maintain written minutes of each meeting.

1.5. The vacancy of any CFIUS-Approved Director position shall be filled within sixty (60) days. The replacement director must satisfy the criteria set forth in Section 1.3 above and must be approved by CFIUS prior to appointment. Removal or replacement of any CFIUS-Approved Director requires prior written approval of CFIUS.

1.6. The Board may include additional directors, including directors nominated by Meridian and management directors, provided that the CFIUS-Approved Directors constitute a majority of the Board at all times. Nothing in this requirement shall restrict the Board from expanding or contracting in total size, so long as the majority requirement is continuously satisfied.

**Requirement 2 --- Government Security Director**

2.1. Saxonbrook shall appoint a Government Security Director (\"GSD\") within thirty (30) days of the Closing Date.

2.2. The GSD must satisfy all of the following criteria:

> \(a\) be a citizen of the United States;
>
> \(b\) hold an active personnel security clearance at the TOP SECRET/SCI level at the time of appointment;
>
> \(c\) be approved in writing by CFIUS prior to appointment; and
>
> \(d\) not be, and not have been within the prior three (3) years, an employee, officer, director, consultant, agent, or representative of Meridian or any affiliate of Meridian.

2.3. The GSD shall report directly and exclusively to the Security Committee of the Board and shall have primary responsibility for: (i) overseeing Saxonbrook\'s day-to-day compliance with the Mitigation Agreement and all applicable security requirements; (ii) serving as Saxonbrook\'s principal liaison with CFIUS, DCSA, and other cognizant security agencies; (iii) managing all aspects of facility security, personnel security, information security, and export control compliance; and (iv) ensuring the integrity of information barriers between Saxonbrook and Meridian at all times.

2.4. The GSD shall have independent authority to deny, restrict, or revoke access by any individual --- including any officer, director, employee, or agent of Saxonbrook or Meridian --- to Classified Information, Classified Spaces, or Export-Controlled Technical Data. Decisions of the GSD regarding access to such information and spaces shall not be subject to review, override, or reversal by the Board, by Meridian, or by any other person or entity, except by CFIUS or the cognizant security agency.

2.5. The GSD shall not be removable from his or her position without the prior written approval of CFIUS. Any request to remove, reassign, or terminate the GSD shall be submitted to CFIUS in writing with a detailed explanation of the reasons for the proposed action. The GSD shall continue to serve in his or her position pending CFIUS\'s written decision on any such request.

2.6. Compensation of the GSD shall be determined by the Security Committee and shall be commensurate with the responsibilities of the position. Compensation of the GSD shall not be subject to approval, influence, or review by Meridian or any Meridian affiliate.

**Requirement 3 --- Voting Trust / Proxy Agreement**

3.1. All shares of Saxonbrook common stock acquired by Meridian in the transaction (5,100,000 shares, representing 51% of the outstanding shares) shall be placed in a voting trust or proxy agreement (the \"Voting Arrangement\") administered by an independent voting trustee approved by CFIUS (the \"Voting Trustee\").

3.2. The Voting Trustee shall exercise all voting rights associated with the shares held in the Voting Arrangement, including but not limited to:

> \(a\) the election and removal of members of the Board of Directors;
>
> \(b\) the approval of mergers, acquisitions, consolidations, dissolutions, or other fundamental corporate transactions;
>
> \(c\) amendments to the certificate of incorporation, bylaws, or other governing documents of Saxonbrook;
>
> \(d\) the approval of equity compensation plans or issuances of additional securities; and
>
> \(e\) all other matters submitted to a vote of shareholders of Saxonbrook.

3.3. The Foreign Acquirer shall retain only economic rights with respect to the shares held in the Voting Arrangement, including the right to receive dividends, distributions, and capital appreciation. The Foreign Acquirer shall have no governance, voting, consent, consultation, information, veto, approval, observer, or other rights that could confer influence or control over the management, operations, strategic direction, or decision-making of Saxonbrook. For the avoidance of doubt, the Foreign Acquirer shall not be entitled to: (i) designate, nominate, or appoint any director or observer to the Board; (ii) receive any non-public information regarding Saxonbrook\'s classified operations, contracts, or programs; (iii) participate in or be consulted regarding any strategic, operational, or business decisions of Saxonbrook beyond those directly affecting the economic value of its shareholding; or (iv) attend or observe meetings of the Board or any committee thereof.

3.4. The Voting Trustee must be a U.S. person or entity organized under the laws of the United States with no current or prior affiliation with Meridian or any affiliate of Meridian. CFIUS must approve the identity of the Voting Trustee in writing prior to the Closing Date.

3.5. The Voting Arrangement shall remain in effect for the entire duration of Meridian\'s direct or indirect ownership interest in Saxonbrook and shall not be terminated, modified, or suspended without the prior written approval of CFIUS.

3.6. The Voting Trustee shall certify to CFIUS on an annual basis, in a written statement delivered no later than thirty (30) days following the end of each calendar year, that the terms of the Voting Arrangement have been observed and that no unauthorized exercise of governance, voting, or other non-economic rights by Meridian has occurred during the reporting period.

**Requirement 4 --- Access Restrictions**

4.1. No Foreign National --- including, without limitation, any employee, officer, director, agent, consultant, contractor, or representative of Meridian or any Meridian affiliate --- may access: (a) Classified Information; (b) Export-Controlled Technical Data; or (c) Classified Spaces within any Saxonbrook facility, without prior written authorization from the appropriate United States Government agency having jurisdiction over such information or space.

4.2. This restriction applies regardless of the nationality of the Foreign National, regardless of any security clearance or access authorization that may have been issued by a foreign government, and regardless of whether any bilateral security agreement or industrial security arrangement exists between the United States and the country of nationality of such Foreign National.

4.3. Saxonbrook shall implement and maintain physical, electronic, and administrative controls to enforce the access restrictions set forth in this Requirement 4, including but not limited to visitor management systems, mandatory escort requirements for all non-cleared personnel in proximity to classified areas, electronic access control lists, and regular audits of access logs.

4.4. The restriction on access to Export-Controlled Technical Data applies to all ITAR-controlled defense articles, defense services, and technical data (22 C.F.R. Parts 120--130), as well as all EAR-controlled items, technology, and software (15 C.F.R. Parts 730--774), whether or not such information is also classified. Access to Export-Controlled Technical Data by any Foreign National is prohibited except as specifically authorized by a valid export license, license exception, or other written authorization issued by the U.S. Department of State, Directorate of Defense Trade Controls, or the U.S. Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry and Security, as applicable.

4.5. Nothing in this Requirement 4 shall be construed to prohibit access by Foreign Nationals to unclassified, non-export-controlled business information of Saxonbrook that does not implicate national security, subject to the information barrier requirements set forth in Requirement 5 below.

**Requirement 5 --- Information Barriers**

5.1. Saxonbrook shall establish and maintain physical and electronic information barriers (\"firewalls\") between its classified and export-controlled operations and Meridian. The purpose of these barriers is to prevent any unauthorized disclosure of Classified Information or Export-Controlled Technical Data to Meridian, its affiliates, or any Foreign National.

5.2. Physical barriers shall include, at a minimum:

> \(a\) controlled access to all classified areas and areas containing Export-Controlled Technical Data, using badge readers, biometric systems, or equivalent access control technology;
>
> \(b\) physical separation of classified work areas and export-controlled work areas from any area accessible to Meridian personnel or other unauthorized individuals; and
>
> \(c\) secure storage of all classified and export-controlled materials in GSA-approved containers or equivalent secure storage, in accordance with NISPOM requirements and DCSA guidance.

5.3

. Electronic barriers shall include, at a minimum:

> \(a\) complete segmentation of all information technology systems and networks used for classified or export-controlled work from any network, system, or platform accessible to Meridian or any Meridian affiliate;
>
> \(b\) prohibition on shared IT infrastructure --- including email servers, cloud computing platforms, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, data analytics tools, and collaborative software --- between Saxonbrook\'s classified or export-controlled operations and Meridian; and
>
> \(c\) implementation of intrusion detection systems, data loss prevention tools, and continuous monitoring on all network boundaries between Saxonbrook\'s internal networks and any external connection.

5.4. The GSD shall have sole authority to approve any exceptions to the information barrier requirements set forth in this Requirement 5, and any such exception shall require prior written approval from CFIUS before implementation.

**Requirement 6 --- Personnel Vetting**

6.1. All members of the Board of Directors, officers, and employees of Saxonbrook who have or will have access to Classified Information or Export-Controlled Technical Data shall undergo enhanced background investigations as directed by DCSA, at Saxonbrook\'s expense. Such investigations shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, any standard personnel security clearance investigation required under the NISPOM.

6.2. CFIUS reserves the right to require the removal of any individual from a position involving access to Classified Information, Classified Spaces, or Export-Controlled Technical Data, upon a determination that such individual poses a risk to national security. Such removal shall be carried out within ten (10) business days of written notice from CFIUS, and the affected individual shall be immediately excluded from all classified and export-controlled work areas pending removal.

6.3. New hires and transferees who will have access to classified programs or Export-Controlled Technical Data must be vetted and, as applicable, granted appropriate security clearances prior to commencing duties in any classified or export-controlled role.

6.4. Saxonbrook shall maintain and provide to DCSA and CFIUS upon request a current and complete roster of all personnel holding security clearances, including the level of clearance, the date of issuance, and the programs to which such personnel have been granted access.

**Requirement 7 --- Technology Control Plan**

7.1. Saxonbrook shall develop a comprehensive Technology Control Plan (\"TCP\") that details the specific measures Saxonbrook will implement to protect Classified Information and Export-Controlled Technical Data from unauthorized access, disclosure, or transfer.

7.2. The TCP shall be developed within sixty (60) days of the Closing Date and submitted to DCSA for review and approval. Saxonbrook shall cooperate fully with DCSA during the review process and shall promptly implement any modifications required by DCSA.

7.3. The TCP shall address, at a minimum:

> \(a\) physical security measures for all facilities containing Classified Information or Export-Controlled Technical Data;
>
> \(b\) electronic and cybersecurity measures, including network segmentation, encryption, and access controls;
>
> \(c\) personnel controls, including identification and authentication procedures, need-to-know determinations, and insider threat detection;
>
> \(d\) visitor access procedures, including procedures for escorted and unescorted access by individuals without appropriate clearances;
>
> \(e\) procedures for handling, storing, transmitting, reproducing, and destroying ITAR- and EAR-controlled materials;
>
> \(f\) procedures for handling, storing, transmitting, reproducing, and destroying classified materials at all classification levels; and
>
> \(g\) reporting procedures for security incidents, including unauthorized access, loss, compromise, or suspected compromise of Classified Information or Export-Controlled Technical Data.

7.4. The TCP shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, or more frequently as required by DCSA, CFIUS, or as circumstances warrant (including in response to security incidents, changes in threat conditions, or modifications to classified programs).

7.5. The GSD shall be responsible for the development, implementation, and ongoing enforcement of the TCP.

**Requirement 8 --- Third-Party Monitor**

8.1. The parties shall engage an independent third-party compliance monitor (the \"Third-Party Monitor\") approved by CFIUS to oversee, evaluate, and verify compliance with the Mitigation Agreement on an ongoing basis.

8.2. The Third-Party Monitor shall be a U.S. person or U.S.-owned entity with demonstrated expertise in national security, facility security, FOCI mitigation, and government compliance matters. The Third-Party Monitor shall have no affiliation, financial interest, or business relationship with either Saxonbrook or Meridian, or with any affiliate, subsidiary, or related entity of either party.

8.3. The Third-Party Monitor shall conduct semiannual compliance audits (every six (6) months) covering all aspects of the Mitigation Agreement, including but not limited to: board composition and Security Committee operations; the GSD\'s activities and independence; the Voting Arrangement; access restrictions and information barriers; the Technology Control Plan; personnel vetting; incident reporting; classified contract continuity; and subcontracting compliance.

8.4. Following the completion of each semiannual audit, the Third-Party Monitor shall deliver written reports to CFIUS within thirty (30) days of each audit completion. The written reports shall include:

> \(a\) a description of the audit scope and methodology;
>
> \(b\) detailed findings regarding compliance with each requirement of the Mitigation Agreement;
>
> \(c\) identification of any deficiencies, areas of concern, or potential violations;
>
> \(d\) recommended corrective actions and timelines for implementation; and
>
> \(e\) an assessment of the overall effectiveness of the mitigation measures.

8.5. Copies of all audit reports shall also be provided to the Security Committee and the GSD contemporaneously with delivery to CFIUS.

8.6. The cost of the Third-Party Monitor --- including all fees, expenses, and costs associated with the conduct of audits and preparation of reports --- shall be borne as agreed by the parties in the Mitigation Agreement.

8.7. CFIUS reserves the right to require replacement of the Third-Party Monitor at any time, upon a determination that the Third-Party Monitor is unable or unwilling to perform its duties effectively, or for any other reason. In the event of replacement, the parties shall engage a successor Third-Party Monitor approved by CFIUS within thirty (30) days.

**Requirement 9 --- Annual Compliance Report**

9.1. Saxonbrook shall prepare and submit to CFIUS a comprehensive annual compliance report covering the prior calendar year.

9.2. The annual compliance report shall be submitted no later than March 31 of each year. This deadline is a fixed date and shall not be subject to extension, deferral, or modification by the parties, the Third-Party Monitor, or any other person or entity without the prior written approval of CFIUS.

9.3. The annual compliance report shall include, at a minimum:

> \(a\) a certification by the GSD and the Chair of the Security Committee that Saxonbrook has complied in all material respects with the Mitigation Agreement during the reporting period;
>
> \(b\) a summary of all compliance activities conducted during the reporting period, including audits, training programs, security upgrades, and self-assessments;
>
> \(c\) a summary of any reportable incidents that occurred during the reporting period and the corrective actions taken in response thereto;
>
> \(d\) a current organizational chart reflecting Board composition, Security Committee membership, the identity of the GSD, and other key personnel;
>
> \(e\) a summary of any changes to classified contracts, including new awards, modifications, extensions, or terminations;
>
> \(f\) financial information sufficient to verify the ongoing viability and financial health of the U.S. Business, including revenue data for classified and unclassified operations; and
>
> \(g\) any other information reasonably requested by CFIUS in advance of the reporting period.

9.4. The annual compliance report shall be signed by the Chief Executive Officer of Saxonbrook and the GSD, certifying the accuracy and completeness of the information contained therein.

9.5. The first annual compliance report shall cover the period from the Closing Date through December 31 of the calendar year in which the Closing occurs.

**Requirement 10 --- Incident Reporting**

10.1. Any actual or suspected breach of the Mitigation Agreement, including but not limited to unauthorized access to Classified Information, Export-Controlled Technical Data, or Classified Spaces, shall be reported to CFIUS within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery.

10.2. For purposes of this Requirement 10, \"discovery\" means the point at which any employee, officer, director, agent, contractor, or representative of Saxonbrook first becomes aware of facts or circumstances that reasonably indicate that a breach has occurred or may have occurred. The obligation to report runs from the time of discovery by any such individual, and shall not be conditioned upon or delayed pending investigation, verification, or determination by the GSD, the Security Committee, or any other person.

10.3. The initial report shall be made in writing to the designated CFIUS monitoring contact (email is acceptable for initial reports). The initial report shall include a preliminary description of the incident, the date and time of discovery, and the identity of the person(s) involved, to the extent known. A detailed written follow-up report shall be submitted to CFIUS within five (5) business days of the initial report.

10.4. The GSD shall be responsible for managing incident response and ensuring that reports are made in a timely manner. However, the reporting obligation is not dependent on the GSD\'s personal awareness; the twenty-four (24) hour clock commences upon discovery by any Saxonbrook personnel.

10.5. Parallel reporting obligations to DCSA, the cognizant security agency, the relevant contracting officer, and any other applicable United States Government agencies shall also be observed in accordance with applicable regulations.

**Requirement 11 --- Government Contracts Continuity**

11.1. Saxonbrook shall maintain all existing classified contracts --- including, without limitation, those associated with Program SENTINEL REACH, Program IRON LATTICE, and Program COBALT MERIDIAN --- without interruption throughout the duration of the Mitigation Agreement.

11.2. Any decision by Saxonbrook to terminate, not rebid, or materially reduce the scope of any classified contract shall require ninety (90) days\' prior written notice directly to CFIUS. Such notice shall be delivered directly to the CFIUS monitoring contact and shall describe in detail the reasons for the proposed action, the impact on classified national defense programs, and the steps Saxonbrook proposes to take to ensure continuity of supply and preservation of classified information.

11.3. During the ninety (90) day notice period, CFIUS may consult with the relevant United States Government contracting agencies and program offices and may direct Saxonbrook to take such steps as CFIUS deems necessary to ensure continuity of supply, preservation of classified information, and protection of national security interests.

11.4. Saxonbrook shall use commercially reasonable efforts to rebid and retain classified contracts upon their expiration or at the conclusion of their current performance periods.

11.5. Nothing in this Requirement 11 shall require Saxonbrook to accept contract terms that are commercially unreasonable, provided that Saxonbrook shall consult with CFIUS before declining to rebid any classified contract.

**Requirement 12 --- Subcontracting Restrictions**

12.1. Saxonbrook shall not subcontract any classified work --- including, without limitation, any work performed under Program SENTINEL REACH, Program IRON LATTICE, or Program COBALT MERIDIAN --- to any Meridian affiliate or any entity in which Meridian holds a ten percent (10%) or greater interest (whether such interest is held directly or indirectly, including through subsidiaries, affiliates, joint ventures, partnerships, or other arrangements) without the prior written approval of CFIUS.

12.2. This restriction applies to all tiers of subcontracting. Saxonbrook shall ensure, through appropriate contractual provisions, that its subcontractors on classified work do not further subcontract classified work to any entity described in Section 12.1 without the prior written approval of CFIUS.

12.3. For purposes of this Requirement 12, \"classified work\" includes any work that requires access to Classified Information or Classified Spaces, or that involves the generation, handling, processing, storage, or transmission of Classified Information.

12.4. Saxonbrook shall maintain and make available to CFIUS and the Third-Party Monitor a current and complete list of all subcontractors performing work on classified contracts, including the name, address, country of organization, and ownership structure of each subcontractor, and a description of the classified work being performed.

**Requirement 13 --- Amendment and Termination**

13.1. **Amendment.** The Mitigation Agreement may only be amended with the prior written consent of all parties to the agreement and CFIUS. No amendment, modification, waiver, or supplement to the Mitigation Agreement shall be effective or enforceable unless it is set forth in a written instrument signed by all parties to the Mitigation Agreement and approved in writing by CFIUS. No waiver of any provision of the Mitigation Agreement shall be effective unless made in writing with the express written consent of CFIUS.

13.2. Duration. The Mitigation Agreement shall remain in force for the duration of Meridian\'s direct or indirect ownership interest in Saxonbrook, whether such interest is held through the Voting Arrangement or otherwise. The obligations of the Mitigation Agreement shall not lapse, expire, or terminate by reason of the passage of time alone.

13.3. Survival. The Mitigation Agreement may survive divestiture by Meridian of its ownership interest in Saxonbrook at CFIUS\'s sole discretion. CFIUS shall determine, in its sole and unreviewable discretion, whether and for how long the obligations of the Mitigation Agreement shall continue following any divestiture, change of control, or other disposition of Meridian\'s direct or indirect interest in Saxonbrook. Without limiting the foregoing, CFIUS may require that some or all obligations of the Mitigation Agreement continue for such period as CFIUS deems necessary to protect national security, including indefinitely, regardless of whether Meridian has divested all of its ownership interest in Saxonbrook.

13.4. **Request for Termination.** The parties may request termination of the Mitigation Agreement by written petition to CFIUS, which shall consider the request in light of the then-current national security circumstances. CFIUS shall not be bound to grant any such request and may impose conditions on any termination.

**Requirement 14 --- Penalties and Enforcement**

14.1. Violation of any term, condition, or requirement of the Mitigation Agreement shall subject the parties to civil penalties pursuant to 50 U.S.C. § 4565(l), including penalties of up to \$250,000 per violation or the value of the transaction, whichever is greater. The value of the transaction for purposes of this provision is \$588,285,000.

14.2. Each day that a violation continues shall constitute a separate violation for purposes of the assessment of civil penalties.

14.3. CFIUS may also seek injunctive relief in any United States district court of competent jurisdiction to compel compliance with the Mitigation Agreement, to prevent any actual or threatened violation, or to obtain any other equitable remedy that the court deems appropriate.

14.4. In addition to civil penalties and injunctive relief, violation of the Mitigation Agreement may result in potential forced divestiture of Meridian\'s ownership interest in Saxonbrook, pursuant to the authority of the President of the United States under 50 U.S.C. § 4565(d)(4). The parties acknowledge that the President retains the authority to direct divestiture of the foreign interest in any covered transaction in order to protect national security.

14.5. The President also retains the authority to take any additional action authorized by law to protect national security, including but not limited to requiring the suspension, modification, or termination of classified contracts, revoking facility security clearances, and imposing such other measures as may be necessary.

14.6. The parties acknowledge and agree that the remedies set forth in this Requirement 14 are cumulative and not exclusive, and that the exercise of any one remedy does not preclude the exercise of any other remedy. The statutory authority of CFIUS and the President is not limited, constrained, or waived by the terms of the Mitigation Agreement.

14.7. Nothing in the Mitigation Agreement shall be construed to waive, limit, or otherwise affect the statutory or regulatory authority of CFIUS, the President, or any other department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States Government to enforce applicable laws and regulations.

**[VI. PROCESS AND TIMELINE]{.underline}**

The parties shall negotiate a Mitigation Agreement that incorporates all of the requirements set forth in Section V above. The parties are expected to work expeditiously and in good faith to complete the negotiation, and are encouraged to engage in frequent consultation with CFIUS during the drafting process.

The executed Mitigation Agreement shall be submitted to CFIUS no later than **May 3, 2025** (thirty (30) calendar days from the issuance of these NST). Submission shall be made in electronic format to the designated CFIUS monitoring contact, with hard copies to follow by courier within five (5) business days.

CFIUS will review the submitted Mitigation Agreement for compliance with these NST and may request revisions, clarifications, or additional provisions as necessary to ensure that the Mitigation Agreement fully satisfies the requirements herein. The parties shall respond promptly to any such requests.

Upon CFIUS\'s determination that the Mitigation Agreement is satisfactory, CFIUS will issue a written clearance of the transaction. Based on the current timeline, CFIUS anticipates that clearance may be issued on or about **May 15, 2025**, subject to the timely submission of a satisfactory Mitigation Agreement and the resolution of any outstanding issues.

The transaction shall not close until CFIUS has issued written clearance. Any attempt to close the transaction prior to the issuance of written clearance by CFIUS shall constitute a violation of the undertakings of the parties and may result in the imposition of penalties and other remedial measures.

The parties are advised to direct all questions regarding the interpretation, application, or implementation of these NST to the designated CFIUS monitoring contact: **Dr. Samuel Keene, Director of Investment Security, Office of Investment Security, U.S. Department of the Treasury**. \(c\) **Management Director.** One (1) management director serving in the capacity described in Section 4.3 (the \"Management

Director\").

In the event of any vacancy among the Meridian-Nominated Directors, Meridian shall nominate a replacement within forty-five (45) days. Each newly appointed director shall satisfy the qualifications applicable to his or her category as set forth above.

The Chief Executive Officer of Saxonbrook shall serve as the Management Director on the Board, serving ex officio for so long as such individual holds the position of CEO. Each Independent U.S. Director shall be subject to initial approval by CFIUS prior to appointment and ongoing approval by CFIUS thereafter. **Section 4.5 --- Security Committee**

The Board shall establish a standing committee to be known as the Security Committee (the \"Security Committee\"), which shall be composed exclusively of the three (3) Independent U.S. Directors. The Security Committee shall have exclusive authority over all matters relating to Saxonbrook\'s classified operations, security policies, compliance with this Agreement, and interactions with DCSA, CFIUS, and other U.S. Government agencies in connection with national security matters. The Security Committee shall meet no less frequently than quarterly and shall maintain minutes of all meetings, which shall be made available to the Third-Party Monitor and, upon request, to CFIUS. The chairperson of the Security Committee shall be selected by a majority vote of the Independent U.S. Directors.

\(c\) Establishing and administering information barriers between Saxonbrook\'s classified operations and Meridian, including the physical and electronic barriers described in Section 9;

\(d\) Conducting periodic internal compliance reviews to assess adherence to the terms of this Agreement and applicable security regulations;

\(e\) Preparing and delivering compliance reports to the Security Committee at each quarterly meeting, covering all material compliance activities, incidents, and areas of concern;

\(f\) Coordinating with the Third-Party Monitor during audits and facilitating the Third-Party Monitor\'s access to facilities, records, and personnel;

\(g\) Maintaining a comprehensive log of all substantive communications between Saxonbrook and Meridian; and

\(h\) Implementing and overseeing the personnel vetting and security clearance procedures described in Section 7.

**Section 5.3 --- Removal**

The Government Security Director may be removed by a unanimous vote of the Security Committee with thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to CFIUS. The Security Committee shall include in such notice the grounds for removal and the identity of the proposed interim or permanent replacement GSD. The removal shall become effective upon the expiration of the thirty-day notice period.

**Section 5.4 --- Vacancy**

In the event the GSD position becomes vacant for any reason, including removal, resignation, death, or incapacity, Saxonbrook shall appoint an interim GSD within fifteen (15) business days of the occurrence of the vacancy. The interim GSD shall satisfy the citizenship and clearance requirements set forth in Section 5.1. Saxonbrook shall submit the name and qualifications of a proposed permanent replacement GSD to CFIUS for approval within forty-five (45) days of the occurrence of the vacancy.

**[SECTION 6: VOTING TRUST AND PROXY ARRANGEMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Establishment of Voting Trust**

All Foreign-Owned Shares, consisting of five million one hundred thousand (5,100,000) shares of Saxonbrook\'s common stock representing fifty-one percent (51%) of the total outstanding shares, shall be placed in a voting trust (the \"Voting Trust\") administered by Clearfield Trust Company as Voting Trustee. The Voting Trust shall be established and fully operative prior to or simultaneously with the Closing. The terms of the Voting Trust are summarized in Exhibit B and are incorporated herein by reference. Meridian\'s rights with respect to the Foreign-Owned Shares shall be limited as follows:

\(a\) **Economic Rights.** Meridian shall retain the right to receive all dividends, distributions, and other economic benefits attributable to the Foreign-Owned Shares, including any capital appreciation realized upon the sale, transfer, or other disposition of such shares, and any proceeds of liquidation or dissolution attributable to such shares. Meridian shall bear all economic risk of loss with respect to the Foreign-Owned Shares.

\(b\) No Voting Rights. Meridian shall have no right to vote the Foreign-Owned Shares on any matter submitted to a vote of Saxonbrook\'s shareholders, including but not limited to the election or removal of directors, approval of mergers or acquisitions, amendments to the certificate of incorporation or bylaws, or any other matter requiring shareholder action. All voting rights with respect to the Foreign-Owned Shares shall be exercised exclusively by the Voting Trustee in its sole discretion, in a manner consistent with the national security interests of the United States and the terms of this Agreement.

\(c\) Consultation Right. Notwithstanding Section 6.1(b), Meridian shall have the right to be consulted by the Voting Trustee in advance of any shareholder vote relating to a proposed sale, merger, consolidation, dissolution, or liquidation of Saxonbrook, or any transaction that would result in a change of control of Saxonbrook (each, a \"Fundamental Transaction\"). When a Fundamental Transaction is proposed, the Voting Trustee shall provide Meridian with reasonable advance notice of the pending vote and an opportunity to submit its views in writing. The Voting Trustee shall consider Meridian\'s views in good faith but shall not be bound thereby and shall retain ultimate discretion over the exercise of voting rights with respect to the Fundamental Transaction.

\(d\) Board Observer. Meridian shall have the right to designate one (1) observer (the \"Board Observer\") to attend all meetings of the Board of Directors of Saxonbrook in a non-voting capacity. The Board Observer shall receive copies of all materials distributed to Board members for Board meetings, except for materials relating to Classified Information, Classified Programs, or matters that the Security Committee determines, in its sole discretion, to involve sensitive national security information. The Board Observer shall be subject to the access restrictions set forth in Section 8 and shall not be present during any portion of a Board meeting at which Classified Information, classified contract performance, classified program details, or other matters designated as restricted by the Security Committee are discussed.

**Section 6.2 --- Voting Trustee Duties**

Clearfield Trust Company, as Voting Trustee, shall exercise all voting rights with respect to the Foreign-Owned Shares in a manner consistent with the national security interests of the United States and the terms of this Agreement. In exercising voting rights, the Voting Trustee shall act independently and shall not take direction from Meridian on any voting matter except as contemplated by Section 6.1(c). The Voting Trustee shall maintain records of all voting actions taken and shall provide quarterly reports to the Security Committee summarizing such actions.

**Section 6.3 --- Voting Trustee Compensation**

The Voting Trustee shall receive an annual fee of One Hundred Eighty Thousand Dollars (\$180,000), payable by Meridian in quarterly installments of Forty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$45,000) each. The Voting Trustee fee shall not be contingent upon any action taken or not taken by the Voting Trustee in the exercise of its duties hereunder.

**Section 6.4 --- Replacement of Voting Trustee**

The Voting Trustee may resign upon ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to Saxonbrook, Meridian, and the Security Committee. A successor Voting Trustee shall be proposed by Saxonbrook and the Security Committee and shall be subject to CFIUS approval prior to assuming the role. In the event of a vacancy in the Voting Trustee position, Saxonbrook and the Security Committee shall propose a replacement within thirty (30) days and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain CFIUS approval as expeditiously as practicable.

**[SECTION 7: PERSONNEL VETTING AND SECURITY CLEARANCES]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Enhanced Background Checks**

All members of the Board of Directors, officers, and employees of Saxonbrook who have access to Classified Programs or Classified Information shall undergo enhanced background checks conducted by or at the direction of the Government Security Director. Such background checks shall include, at a minimum, a review of financial records, foreign travel history, foreign contacts, and any other information relevant to the individual\'s suitability for access to classified information and facilities. Enhanced background checks shall be in addition to, and shall not substitute for, any investigation conducted by DCSA in connection with security clearance applications under the NISPOM.

**Section 7.2 --- CFIUS Removal Right**

CFIUS retains the right, at any time during the term of this Agreement, to require the removal of any individual Board member, officer, or employee of Saxonbrook upon a determination by CFIUS that such individual poses a risk to the national security of the United States. Saxonbrook shall comply with any such requirement within thirty (30) days of receipt of written notice from CFIUS specifying the individual to be removed and the general basis for the determination, to the extent such basis may be disclosed consistent with applicable law.

**Section 7.3 --- Meridian-Nominated Director Vetting**

Each Meridian-Nominated Director shall undergo an enhanced background check prior to initial appointment to the Board and annually thereafter during the term of such director\'s service. Background check results shall be made available to the Security Committee and, upon request, to CFIUS. The GSD shall coordinate the conduct of such background checks and shall maintain records of all vetting activities.

**Section 7.4 --- Personnel Security Clearances**

Saxonbrook shall maintain active personnel security clearances for all employees requiring access to Classified Information in the performance of their duties. As of the anticipated Effective Date, Saxonbrook employs one thousand one hundred eighty (1,180) personnel with active clearances out of a total workforce of two thousand three hundred forty (2,340). Saxonbrook shall promptly report any adverse clearance actions, including denials, revocations, and suspensions, to the GSD and DCSA in accordance with applicable regulations.

**[SECTION 8: ACCESS RESTRICTIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Foreign National Access Restrictions**

No Foreign National, including any employee, officer, director, agent, consultant, or representative of Meridian or any affiliate of Meridian, shall have access to Classified Information or Classified Facilities of Saxonbrook without prior authorization from the appropriate United States Government authority in accordance with applicable regulations, including NISPOM requirements governing foreign national access to classified information and the terms of any applicable international security agreement. Access by any Foreign National to Classified Facilities shall require advance coordination with the GSD and compliance with the escort and access control procedures established pursuant to Section 8.3. The foregoing restriction shall apply at all times during the term of this Agreement and shall be administered by the GSD.

**Section 8.2 --- Board Observer Access Limitations**

The Board Observer designated by Meridian pursuant to Section 6.1(d) shall not be permitted to access Classified Information or enter Classified Facilities under any circumstances. The Board Observer shall be required to leave any Board meeting, or any portion thereof, during which Classified Information, classified contract performance, classified program details, or other matters designated as restricted by the Security Committee are discussed. The GSD shall establish procedures to ensure that the Board Observer is provided with adequate notice of restricted portions of Board meetings and is escorted from the meeting room prior to any discussion of restricted matters.

**Section 8.3 --- Visitor and Contractor Access**

Any visitor or contractor seeking access to Saxonbrook\'s facilities shall be subject to access control procedures established by the GSD and approved by the Security Committee. All visitors and contractors shall be required to sign in and out at the front security desk and to display visitor badges at all times while on Saxonbrook\'s premises. Foreign National visitors shall be escorted at all times within non-classified areas by a Saxonbrook employee holding an appropriate security clearance and shall be prohibited from entering classified areas. The GSD shall maintain a log of all Foreign National visits, which shall be made available to the Third-Party Monitor and, upon request, to CFIUS.

**[SECTION 9: INFORMATION BARRIERS AND TECHNOLOGY CONTROLS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Physical Information Barriers**

Saxonbrook shall establish and maintain physical information barriers (\"firewalls\") between its classified operations and Meridian. Physical barriers shall include, at a minimum, the following measures:

\(a\) Restricted access areas within Saxonbrook\'s Huntsville headquarters at 4700 Redstone Gateway Blvd., Suite 300, Huntsville, Alabama 35808, and any other facility where classified work is performed, delineated by physical barriers such as walls, locked doors, and controlled entry points;

\(b\) Separate entrances, badge systems, and access controls for classified and unclassified areas, ensuring that access to classified spaces is limited to personnel with appropriate security clearances and a demonstrated need to know;

\(c\) Secure storage for classified materials, including approved GSA security containers and vault-type rooms, maintained in accordance with NISPOM requirements and DCSA directives; and

\(d\) Designated secure conference rooms for discussions involving Classified Information, equipped with appropriate countermeasures and sound attenuation.

**Section 9.2 --- Electronic Information Barriers**

Saxonbrook shall establish and maintain electronic information barriers, including the following measures:

\(a\) Complete logical and physical separation of all information technology systems used for classified operations from all Meridian-connected networks, including Meridian\'s corporate intranet, email systems, file-sharing platforms, and any other electronic communication infrastructure;

\(b\) A prohibition on any direct or indirect network connectivity, including via the Internet or virtual private network, between Saxonbrook\'s classified IT systems and any Meridian system, whether located in the United States or abroad;

\(c\) Segmentation of Saxonbrook\'s unclassified IT systems to prevent the unauthorized transfer of sensitive but unclassified information to Meridian, including the implementation of data loss prevention tools, email filtering, and access controls on shared drives and cloud-based storage.

Physical security upgrades to the Huntsville facility, including the installation of additional controlled-access barriers, badge readers, and intrusion detection systems, shall be completed within one hundred twenty (120) days of the Closing Date. The estimated cost of compliance measures under this Section 9 is as follows: IT segmentation and network hardening, Five Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars (\$520,000); personnel vetting enhancements, Three Hundred Ten Thousand Dollars (\$310,000); and physical security upgrades, Three Hundred Seventy Thousand Dollars (\$370,000), for a total estimated annual compliance cost of One Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,200,000).

**Section 9.3 --- Communications Protocols**

All communications between Saxonbrook personnel engaged in classified operations and Meridian, including the Meridian-Nominated Directors and the Board Observer, shall be conducted through the GSD or the GSD\'s designee, except for communications relating solely to routine unclassified corporate matters such as financial reporting and human resources administration. No Classified Information or sensitive technical data relating to the Classified Programs shall be transmitted to Meridian through any channel, whether electronic, oral, or written. The GSD shall maintain a detailed log of all substantive communications with Meridian, which shall be made available to the Third-Party Monitor and CFIUS upon request.

**Section 9.4 --- Technology Control Plan**

Saxonbrook shall develop a Technology Control Plan (\"TCP\") in accordance with DCSA requirements and consistent with the provisions of this Agreement. The TCP shall be submitted to DCSA for review within ninety (90) days of the Effective Date. The TCP shall set forth detailed procedures for the safeguarding of classified and sensitive information, the administration of physical and electronic information barriers, personnel access controls, and the handling of export-controlled materials. Saxonbrook shall implement the TCP promptly upon DCSA approval and shall maintain compliance with the TCP at all times during the term of this Agreement. The TCP shall be subject to periodic review and update as necessary to address changes in Saxonbrook\'s operations, threat environment, or applicable regulatory requirements.

**Section 9.5 --- TCP Contents**

The Technology Control Plan shall address, at a minimum, the following subjects:

\(a\) Procedures for the handling, safeguarding, storage, and destruction of Classified Information and materials bearing special access program caveats;

\(b\) Electronic security measures, including network segmentation architecture, access control lists, encryption protocols, intrusion detection and prevention systems, and audit logging;

\(c\) Physical security measures, including facility layout, access control points, badge and biometric systems, alarm systems, and secure storage;

\(d\) Personnel security protocols, including access authorization procedures, need-to-know determinations, and procedures for processing new clearance applications and reporting adverse actions;

\(e\) Training requirements for all personnel with access to Classified Information, including initial onboarding training and annual refresher training;

\(f\) Incident response procedures, including procedures for the identification, containment, investigation, and remediation of security incidents; and

\(g\) Audit and monitoring mechanisms, including internal self-assessment schedules and procedures for facilitating external audits by the Third-Party Monitor and CFIUS.

**[SECTION 10: GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS CONTINUITY]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Maintenance of Contracts**

Saxonbrook shall maintain all existing classified contracts, including SENTINEL REACH (annual revenue: approximately Eighty-Seven Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$87,400,000)), IRON LATTICE (annual revenue: approximately One Hundred Thirty-Four Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$134,200,000)), and COBALT MERIDIAN (annual revenue: approximately Ninety Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$90,400,000)), without interruption throughout the term of this Agreement. Saxonbrook shall use commercially reasonable efforts to continue performance under all such contracts in accordance with their respective terms and conditions, applicable federal acquisition regulations, and any directives from the contracting officers or cognizant government agencies.

**Section 10.2 --- Contract Termination or Non-Rebid Notice**

In the event Saxonbrook proposes to terminate, not renew, or decline to submit a proposal for rebid of any classified contract, Saxonbrook shall provide sixty (60) days\' prior written notice to the Security Committee, which shall promptly inform CFIUS. Such notice shall include the identity of the classified contract at issue, the grounds for the proposed termination, non-renewal, or decision not to rebid, the estimated impact on Saxonbrook\'s classified workforce and facility security posture, and any alternative arrangements proposed by Saxonbrook to ensure continuity of the government\'s interests.

**Section 10.3 --- New Classified Contracts**

Saxonbrook may pursue new classified contracts in the ordinary course of business, consistent with its capabilities, facility security clearance, and applicable procurement regulations. Any new classified contract that would materially alter Saxonbrook\'s security posture, facility clearance requirements, or the scope of classified operations shall be reported to the Security Committee and the GSD within thirty (30) days of contract award.

**[SECTION 11: SUBCONTRACTING RESTRICTIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- General Prohibition**

Saxonbrook shall not subcontract any classified work to any entity located outside of the United States without the prior written approval of CFIUS.

**Section 11.2 --- Meridian Affiliate Prohibition**

Saxonbrook shall not subcontract any classified work to Meridian or any direct or indirect subsidiary, affiliate, or parent company of Meridian, regardless of whether such entity is located within or outside the United States.

**Section 11.3 --- Related Entity Restriction**

Saxonbrook shall not subcontract any classified work to any entity in which Meridian holds a twenty-five percent (25%) or greater direct equity interest without the prior written approval of CFIUS. For purposes of this Section 11.3, \"direct equity interest\" means a direct ownership interest in the equity securities of the entity, as reflected on Meridian\'s books and records. Prior to awarding any subcontract for classified work, Saxonbrook shall verify, through the GSD, that the proposed subcontractor does not fall within the prohibitions set forth in this Section 11.3 or Section 11.2.

**Section 11.4 --- Reporting**

Saxonbrook shall maintain a current and comprehensive list of all subcontractors performing work on class

ified contracts, including the name, address, and ownership structure of each subcontractor and a description of the classified work being performed. This list shall be updated at least quarterly and shall be made available to the Third-Party Monitor for review during each audit and, upon request, to CFIUS.

**[SECTION 12: MONITORING AND COMPLIANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Third-Party Monitor Audits**

The Third-Party Monitor, Pinnacle Security Consultants, Inc., shall conduct annual compliance audits of Saxonbrook\'s adherence to the terms of this Agreement. Each audit shall encompass all material aspects of this Agreement, including but not limited to governance and board composition, voting trust operations, access restrictions and information barriers, personnel vetting and security clearance management, classified contract management, incident reporting, export control compliance, and the implementation of the Technology Control Plan. The Third-Party Monitor shall have unrestricted access to all relevant records, documents, facilities, and personnel necessary to conduct a thorough and meaningful audit, subject to applicable security clearance requirements.

**Section 12.2 --- Monitor Reports**

Following each audit, the Third-Party Monitor shall prepare a comprehensive written report summarizing its findings, including any instances of non-compliance, areas of concern, potential vulnerabilities, and recommendations for remediation. The Third-Party Monitor shall deliver copies of each report to the Security Committee and CFIUS. The report shall include a compliance rating for each major area of the Agreement, a summary of corrective actions recommended and the timeline for implementation, and a comparison with findings from any prior audit to track trends and assess progress on previously identified remediation items.

**Section 12.3 --- Annual Compliance Report**

Saxonbrook shall prepare and submit to CFIUS a comprehensive annual compliance report covering the prior calendar year. Such report shall be submitted within ninety (90) days following the end of each calendar year, or such later date as agreed by the Third-Party Monitor. The annual compliance report shall be in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit E and shall include, at a minimum, the following:

\(a\) A summary of all material compliance activities undertaken during the reporting period;

\(b\) A certification by the Government Security Director of compliance with the Technology Control Plan;

\(c\) A report on personnel security clearance activity, including new clearances granted, clearances revoked or suspended, and the current clearance population;

\(d\) A summary of any Reportable Incidents during the reporting period and the status of any remediation actions;

\(e\) Financial statements certified by Ashford & Lyle, PA, Saxonbrook\'s independent auditor, to the extent relevant to compliance costs incurred under this Agreement; and

\(f\) A certification by the CEO and General Counsel of Saxonbrook attesting to the accuracy and completeness of the report.

**Section 12.4 --- Third-Party Monitor Compensation**

Pinnacle Security Consultants, Inc. shall receive an annual fee of Four Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$475,000), payable by Saxonbrook in quarterly installments of One Hundred Eighteen Thousand Seven Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$118,750). The fee shall be reviewed annually and adjusted by mutual agreement of Saxonbrook and the Third-Party Monitor, subject to reasonableness.

**Section 12.5 --- CFIUS Access Rights**

CFIUS and its designees shall have the right, at any time during the term of this Agreement and upon reasonable notice, to:

\(a\) Inspect Saxonbrook\'s facilities, including classified and unclassified areas;

\(b\) Review records, documents, and communications related to this Agreement, the TCP, and Saxonbrook\'s compliance activities;

\(c\) Interview Board members, officers, employees, and the GSD; and

\(d\) Conduct its own independent compliance review, separate from and in addition to the audits conducted by the Third-Party Monitor.

Saxonbrook shall cooperate fully with CFIUS in connection with any such inspection, review, or interview.

**[SECTION 13: INFORMATION SHARING WITH CFIUS]{.underline}**

**Section 13.1 --- Ongoing Reporting Obligations**

Saxonbrook shall provide CFIUS with prompt written notice of the following events:

\(a\) Any material change to Saxonbrook\'s ownership structure, including any acquisition, disposition, or transfer of shares by Meridian or any other significant shareholder;

\(b\) Any change in Board composition, including the appointment, resignation, or removal of any director;

\(c\) Any change in the Government Security Director, including any vacancy, interim appointment, or permanent replacement;

\(d\) Any material change in Saxonbrook\'s facility security posture, including any upgrade or downgrade of its facility security clearance or any change in the accreditation status of its classified facilities; and

\(e\) Any new classified contract award or material modification to an existing classified contract, including changes in classification level, scope of work, or contract value exceeding ten percent (10%).

**Section 13.2 --- CFIUS Inquiries**

Saxonbrook and Meridian shall respond to any inquiry from CFIUS within ten (10) business days of receipt, or within such shorter period as CFIUS may specify for matters involving classified programs, imminent national security concerns, or other exigent circumstances. All responses shall be in writing and shall be delivered to the CFIUS Monitoring Agency at the address set forth in Section 18.3.

**[SECTION 14: INCIDENT REPORTING]{.underline}**

**Section 14.1 --- Reportable Incidents**

A \"Reportable Incident\" shall include, without limitation, any of the following:

\(a\) Any actual or suspected unauthorized access to Classified Information or Classified Facilities by any Foreign National, including any employee, officer, director, or agent of Meridian;

\(b\) Any actual or suspected breach of the physical or electronic information barriers established pursuant to Section 9 of this Agreement;

\(c\) Any actual or suspected violation of any provision of this Agreement by any Party or any individual subject to this Agreement;

\(d\) Any actual or suspected unauthorized transfer, disclosure, or export of export-controlled technical data, including data subject to the ITAR or EAR, to any unauthorized person or entity; and

\(e\) Any compromise or suspected compromise of Classified Information, including loss, theft, or unauthorized destruction of classified materials.

**Section 14.2 --- Reporting Timeline**

Upon the occurrence of a Reportable Incident, Saxonbrook shall report such incident to CFIUS within seventy-two (72) hours of the date on which the Government Security Director determines that a Reportable Incident has occurred. The GSD shall conduct a preliminary assessment upon becoming aware of facts or circumstances that may constitute a Reportable Incident and shall make a determination as to whether a Reportable Incident has occurred as promptly as practicable. The 72-hour reporting clock shall commence upon the GSD\'s affirmative determination. In addition to reporting to CFIUS, Saxonbrook shall simultaneously report the incident to DCSA to the extent required by applicable NISPOM provisions.

**Section 14.3 --- Report Contents**

Each incident report submitted to CFIUS under this Section 14 shall include the following:

\(a\) The date and time of the incident;

\(b\) The date and time the incident was discovered and by whom;

\(c\) The nature and circumstances of the incident, including a detailed factual narrative;

\(d\) The individuals involved or potentially involved;

\(e\) The Classified Information or Classified Programs potentially affected;

\(f\) Corrective actions taken or planned to prevent recurrence; and

\(g\) The GSD\'s assessment of the severity and potential impact of the incident on national security.

**Section 14.4 --- Preservation of Evidence**

Saxonbrook shall preserve all records, logs, electronic data, surveillance footage, and other evidence related to any Reportable Incident for a minimum of five (5) years from the date of the incident. Such preservation obligation shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

**[SECTION 15: EXPORT CONTROL COMPLIANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 15.1 --- ITAR Compliance**

Saxonbrook shall maintain compliance with the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (\"ITAR\"), 22 C.F.R. Parts 120--130, with respect to all defense articles, defense services, and related technical data within the scope of its operations. Saxonbrook shall not export or transfer any ITAR-controlled item, technical data, or defense service to Meridian or to any Foreign National without a valid license, agreement, or other written authorization from the Directorate of Defense Trade Controls (\"DDTC\") of the U.S. Department of State. Saxonbrook shall maintain an internal ITAR compliance program that includes designated compliance officers, written procedures, employee training, and recordkeeping.

**Section 15.2 --- EAR Compliance**

Saxonbrook shall maintain compliance with the Export Administration Regulations (\"EAR\"), 15 C.F.R. Parts 730--774, with respect to all dual-use items, software, and technology within the scope of its operations. Saxonbrook shall not export or transfer any EAR-controlled item to any person or entity without ensuring that all applicable license requirements have been satisfied.

**Section 15.3 --- Export Screening**

Saxonbrook shall screen all proposed transfers of technical data or technology to Foreign Nationals, including Meridian personnel, the Board Observer, and Meridian-Nominated Directors who are Foreign Nationals, against applicable export control lists, including the United States Munitions List (\"USML\"), the Commerce Control List (\"CCL\"), and the Treasury Department\'s list of Specially Designated Nationals (\"SDN List\"). Saxonbrook shall obtain all necessary authorizations prior to any such transfer.

**[SECTION 16: TRAINING AND AWARENESS]{.underline}**

**Section 16.1 --- Security Training**

Saxonbrook shall provide initial and annual security training to all Board members, officers, and employees regarding the following subjects:

\(a\) The terms and requirements of this Agreement;

\(b\) Classification policies and procedures, including proper marking, handling, storage, and destruction of classified materials;

\(c\) Access restrictions applicable to Foreign Nationals, including the prohibitions set forth in Section 8;

\(d\) Information barrier protocols established pursuant to Section 9;

\(e\) Incident reporting procedures, including the definition of a Reportable Incident and the reporting obligations set forth in Section 14; and

\(f\) Export control requirements under the ITAR and EAR, including deemed export rules applicable to Foreign Nationals in the workplace.

Training records shall be maintained by the GSD and made available to the Third-Party Monitor during each audit.

**Section 16.2 --- Meridian Training**

Meridian shall ensure that all of its personnel who have any interaction with Saxonbrook, including the Board Observer, Meridian-Nominated Directors, and any Meridian corporate staff involved in oversight of Meridian\'s investment in Saxonbrook, receive training on the access restrictions and information barriers established by this Agreement. Such training shall be conducted prior to any such individual\'s initial interaction with Saxonbrook and shall be refreshed annually. Meridian shall certify to the GSD and the Security Committee on an annual basis that such training has been completed.

**[SECTION 17: REMEDIES AND PENALTIES]{.underline}**

**Section 17.1 --- Penalties for Violations**

Any violation of this Agreement shall subject the Parties to civil penalties as provided under 50 U.S.C. § 4565(l), including penalties not to exceed Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000) per violation. In addition, the Parties acknowledge that CFIUS or any other agency of the United States Government may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to enforce the terms of this Agreement. The Parties further acknowledge that violations of this Agreement may result in referral to the U.S. Department of Justice for enforcement action and may adversely affect Saxonbrook\'s facility security clearance and eligibility for classified contracts.

**Section 17.2 --- Cure Period**

Upon receipt of written notice from CFIUS of an alleged violation, the Party or Parties in alleged violation shall have thirty (30) days to cure such violation to the satisfaction of CFIUS, unless the violation involves an imminent threat to the national security of the United States, in which case CFIUS may require immediate corrective action. The cure period may be extended by CFIUS in its discretion upon a showing of good cause by the Party seeking the extension. Failure to cure a violation within the applicable cure period shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement.

**Section 17.3 --- Reservation of Rights**

Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to limit the authority of CFIUS or the President of the United States under 50 U.S.C. § 4565 to take any action authorized by law, including but not limited to suspending or prohibiting the Transaction. All statutory and regulatory remedies available to the United States Government are expressly preserved. The Parties acknowledge that the provisions of this Section 17 are in addition to, and not in limitation of, any other rights or remedies available to CFIUS or the United States Government under applicable law.

**[SECTION 18: AMENDMENT, TERMINATION, AND GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 18.1 --- Amendments**

This Agreement may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by the authorized representatives of Saxonbrook, Meridian, and the Voting Trustee. Any such amendment shall be effective only upon execution by all such parties and delivery to each Party. No oral modification of any provision of this Agreement shall be valid or enforceable.

**Section 18.2 --- Term and Termination**

This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall remain in full force and effect for the duration of Meridian\'s ownership interest in Saxonbrook. This Agreement shall terminate automatically upon the complete divestiture of Meridian\'s ownership interest in Saxonbrook, subject to a twelve (12)-month wind-down period during which Sections 8 (Access Restrictions), 9 (Information Barriers and Technology Controls), 12 (Monitoring and Compliance), and 14 (Incident Reporting) shall remain in effect. Upon expiration of the twelve-month wind-down period, all obligations under this Agreement shall cease, and the Parties shall have no further duties or liabilities hereunder except for obligations that expressly survive termination. For the avoidance of doubt, the twelve-month wind-down period shall commence on the date of the completion of Meridian\'s divestiture and shall expire automatically on the twelve-month anniversary of such date.

**[EXHIBIT C: INFORMATION BARRIER PROTOCOLS]{.underline}**

**Detailed Protocols for Physical and Electronic Information Barriers**

The following protocols are established pursuant to Section 9 of the Agreement and shall be implemented and maintained by Saxonbrook under the oversight of the Government Security Director and the Security Committee. These protocols shall be supplemented by the Technology Control Plan upon its development and approval by DCSA.

**I. Physical Barriers**

*A. Classified Areas*

Saxonbrook\'s Huntsville headquarters at 4700 Redstone Gateway Blvd., Suite 300, Huntsville, Alabama 35808, contains both classified and unclassified workspaces. The classified areas include the Classified Programs Operations Center (CPOC), secure vaults and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs), and classified document storage rooms. These areas are physically separated from unclassified areas by reinforced walls, sound-attenuated barriers, and controlled-access entry points.

*B. Access Control Procedures*

Access to classified areas shall be controlled by the following mechanisms:

\(a\) Badge-controlled entry using proximity card readers, supplemented by biometric authentication (fingerprint or iris scan) at all entry points to SCIFs and vault areas;

\(b\) A mantrap entry system at the primary entrance to the CPOC;

\(c\) Visitor logs maintained at each classified area entry point, recording the name, organization, clearance level, purpose of visit, and time of entry and departure for each individual;

\(d\) Closed-circuit television (CCTV) monitoring of all entry points and common areas within and adjacent to classified spaces, with recordings retained for a minimum of ninety (90) days.

*C. Segregation of Workspaces*

Classified and unclassified workspaces shall be physically segregated such that personnel working on classified programs do not share office space, conference rooms, or common areas with Meridian personnel, the Board Observer, or any Foreign National. Separate break rooms and restrooms shall be designated for classified area personnel during periods of heightened security operations.

*D. Secure Conference Rooms*

At least two (2) secure conference rooms shall be maintained within the classified area for meetings involving Classified Information. These rooms shall be equipped with appropriate countermeasures, including radio-frequency shielding, sound masking, and visual privacy measures.

**II. Electronic Barriers**

*A. Network Architecture*

Saxonbrook\'s classified IT systems shall be completely separated, both logically and physically, from all unclassified systems. The classified network shall not share any hardware, software, cabling, or infrastructure with the corporate unclassified network or any Meridian-connected system. Air-gapping shall be maintained between classified and unclassified environments.

*B. Prohibition on Removable Media Transfer*

No removable media (including USB drives, external hard drives, CDs, DVDs, or memory cards) shall be transferred between classified and unclassified environments without the prior written authorization of the GSD and in compliance with DCSA-approved procedures for cross-domain transfer.

*C. Email and Data Loss Prevention*

Saxonbrook\'s unclassified email system shall be equipped with data loss prevention (DLP) filters designed to detect and prevent the unauthorized transmission of classified or sensitive information to Meridian email domains or other external recipients. The DLP system shall be configured to quarantine and flag for manual review any outbound email containing keywords, file types, or markings associated with classified programs.

*D. Separate Server Infrastructure*

All classified data shall be stored on dedicated, separately maintained servers located within accredited classified spaces. No classified data shall be stored on cloud-based platforms or servers accessible to Meridian.

**III. Personnel Controls**

\(a\) A clear-desk policy shall be enforced in all classified areas;

\(b\) Personal electronic devices, including mobile phones, smartwatches, tablets, and laptops, shall be prohibited within classified areas and shall be stored in designated lockers prior to entry;

\(c\) All communications between Saxonbrook employees and Meridian personnel shall be routed through the GSD or the GSD\'s designee, as set forth in Section 9.3 of the Agreement.

**IV. Audit Trail**

All access to classified areas shall be logged electronically. Electronic access logs shall be preserved for a minimum of five (5) years and shall be made available to the Third-Party Monitor during each audit and, upon request, to CFIUS. The GSD shall review access logs on at least a monthly basis to identify any anomalies or unauthorized access attempts.

**IV. Audit Methodology**

Each audit shall employ the following methodology:
