He is responsible for all legal affairs of the Company, including contracts, regulatory compliance, export control matters, and liaison with outside counsel.

**Chief Financial Officer.** Brian Etcheverry --- U.S. citizen, holding an active SECRET personnel security clearance. Mr. Etcheverry reports to the CEO and is responsible for all financial operations, including budgeting, financial reporting, audit coordination, and treasury management.

**Chief Technology Officer.** Dr. Lena Suresh --- U.S. citizen, holding an active TOP SECRET/SCI personnel security clearance. Dr. Suresh reports to the CEO and oversees all classified and unclassified research and development programs, including the SENTINEL REACH, IRON LATTICE, and COBALT MERIDIAN programs described in Section 7 below.

**Facility Security Officer (FSO). Colonel (Ret.) Marcus Delaney, USAF --- U.S. citizen, holding an active TOP SECRET/SCI personnel security clearance. Colonel Delaney reports to the CEO and to the Security Committee of the Board. He is responsible for National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (\"NISPOM\") compliance, personnel clearance processing, classified facility operations, and physical security at all Saxonbrook facilities.**

**Government Security Director (GSD).** This position is to be established under the Mitigation Agreement. The GSD will report directly to the Security Committee of the Board. The proposed candidate is pending CFIUS approval. The GSD will oversee FOCI mitigation compliance, serve as the primary interface with DCSA and CFIUS on all security matters, and manage the development and implementation of the Technology Control Plan (\"TCP\").

**Third-Party Monitor. The proposed Third-Party Monitor is Pinnacle Security Consultants, Inc. (Principal: Rear Admiral Constance \"Connie\" Vega, USN (Ret.)), located at 1550 Crystal Drive, Suite 420, Arlington, VA 22202. Pinnacle will conduct periodic compliance audits and submit reports to CFIUS and the Security Committee. The annual monitoring fee is \$475,000, payable by Saxonbrook. The annual fee for the Voting Trustee (Clearfield Trust Company) is \$180,000, payable by Meridian.**

**[Section 6: Facility Security Clearance (FCL) Profile]{.underline}**

**FCL Level. Saxonbrook holds a Facility Clearance (\"FCL\") at the TOP SECRET level.**

**Cognizant Security Agency. The cognizant security agency for Saxonbrook is the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (\"DCSA\"), which administers the National Industrial Security Program (\"NISP\") and oversees Saxonbrook\'s compliance with the NISPOM (32 C.F.R. Part 117).**

**FOCI Status. Saxonbrook is currently not under Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (\"FOCI\"). Upon consummation of the proposed Meridian acquisition --- in which Meridian would acquire 51% of Saxonbrook\'s outstanding common stock --- Saxonbrook will be subject to FOCI due to Meridian\'s controlling foreign ownership interest. As a result, a FOCI mitigation instrument will be required to maintain Saxonbrook\'s FCL.**

**Proposed FOCI Mitigation Instrument. The FOCI mitigation framework contemplates a Voting Trust Agreement / Proxy Agreement structure. Under the Security Control Agreement component of the Mitigation Agreement, Meridian\'s 51% shares will be held in a voting trust by Clearfield Trust Company, with Meridian retaining only eco

nomic rights. This arrangement is designed to negate Meridian\'s ability to exercise ownership, control, or influence over Saxonbrook\'s management, operations, or access to classified information.**

**Safeguarding. Saxonbrook maintains an approved Facility Security Plan and a NISPOM-compliant security infrastructure at its Huntsville headquarters campus. The Company\'s security program is administered by the FSO, Colonel (Ret.) Marcus Delaney, and will be further overseen by the Government Security Director following the GSD\'s appointment.**

**Cleared Facility Areas.** The Huntsville campus includes two principal cleared areas:

> • **Building A** --- Main operations facility; cleared for operations at **SECRET** and below.
>
> • **Building C** --- Classified research and development facility; cleared for operations at **SECRET** and **TOP SECRET/SCI**, including a DCSA-accredited SCIF.

Both buildings are located at 4700 Redstone Gateway Blvd., Huntsville, AL 35808.

**Cleared Personnel.** Of the Company\'s 2,340 total employees, approximately 1,180 hold active personnel security clearances (50.4% of the workforce). The clearance breakdown is as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Clearance Level**                 **Number of Personnel**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  TOP SECRET/SCI                      \~85

  TOP SECRET                          \~340

  SECRET                              \~755

  **Total Cleared**                   **\~1,180**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Physical Security Upgrades.** Under Section 9.2 of the Mitigation Agreement, certain physical security upgrades to the Huntsville facility are required to be completed within 120 days of the closing date.

**Estimated Annual Compliance Cost.** The estimated annual cost of FOCI mitigation compliance measures is approximately \$1,200,000, broken down as follows: IT segmentation and cybersecurity measures --- \$520,000; personnel vetting and security clearance administration --- \$310,000; physical security upgrades and maintenance --- \$370,000.

**[Section 7: Classified Programs Summary]{.underline}**

Saxonbrook holds active classified contracts with the U.S. Department of Defense that generated \$312,000,000 in revenue during FY 2024, representing approximately 64.3% of Saxonbrook\'s total annual revenue (\$312.0M of \$485.0M). The Company currently performs work on three active classified programs, as detailed in the table below:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Program Name**   **Classification Level**   **Description**                                                **FY 2024 Revenue**
  ------------------ -------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------
  SENTINEL REACH     TOP SECRET/SCI             Next-generation inertial navigation for hypersonic platforms   \$87,400,000

  IRON LATTICE       SECRET                     Sensor array integration for destroyer-class vessels           \$134,200,000

  COBALT MERIDIAN    SECRET                     Precision guidance components for air-launched munitions       \$90,400,000

  **Total**                                                                                                    **\$312,000,000**
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Revenue from these three classified programs constitutes the overwhelming majority of Saxonbrook\'s defense-related revenue and is the primary national security concern driving CFIUS\'s mitigation requirements for the proposed Meridian acquisition. The loss or compromise of any of these programs --- or the unauthorized disclosure of the classified and controlled technical data associated with them --- would represent a significant national security risk.

**Export Control Classification**

All three programs involve **ITAR-controlled technical data** and **EAR-controlled components**. The specific export control classifications are as follows:

> • **SENTINEL REACH** involves articles and technical data controlled under ITAR Category XI(a) (military electronics) and Category XII(d) (fire control, range finder, optical and guidance and control equipment), as well as associated EAR-controlled components and technology.
>
> • **IRON LATTICE** involves articles and technical data controlled under ITAR Category IV (launch vehicles, guided missiles, ballistic missiles, rockets, torpedoes, bombs, and mines) and associated technical data under ITAR Category IV(h).
>
> • **COBALT MERIDIAN** involves articles and technical data controlled under ITAR Category IV and associated technical data, including precision guidance component specifications and performance parameters.

**ITAR/EAR-Controlled Unclassified Technical Data**

A substantial volume of Saxonbrook\'s technical data is subject to ITAR and EAR export controls even when the underlying information is unclassified. This body of controlled but unclassified data includes, without limitation: engineering drawings and specifications; test data and test reports; manufacturing process specifications and quality assurance records; performance parameters and modeling data; software source code and algorithms used in guidance and navigation subsystems; and technical correspondence with DoD program offices.

Much of this ITAR/EAR-controlled but unclassified technical data is stored on Saxonbrook\'s general engineering network --- a network that is separate from the classified IT systems but is accessible to the approximately 1,160 uncleared employees who are U.S. persons. The general engineering network is not currently subject to the same access restrictions that apply to classified systems, because under Saxonbrook\'s current operating posture (with no FOCI), all employees with access to this network are U.S. persons, and no export authorization is required for U.S. person access to ITAR- or EAR-controlled data.

**Implications for the FOCI Mitigation Framework**

The NST issued on April 3, 2025, addresses this concern directly. Requirement 4 of the NST restricts foreign national access to both \"classified information\" and \"export-controlled technical data (ITAR/EAR).\" This dual scope is significant because Saxonbrook holds a substantial volume of ITAR/EAR-controlled data that is not classified. Any mitigation framework must address access to both categories --- classified information and unclassified but export-controlled technical data --- to fully satisfy the NST.

A mitigation framework that restricts access only to classified information and classified facilities, without separately addressing access to ITAR/EAR-controlled unclassified technical data, would leave a significant gap. In such a scenario, Meridian personnel (who are non-U.S. persons under ITAR and EAR) could potentially access controlled technical data on the general engineering network without triggering a violation of the Mitigation Agreement, if the Agreement\'s access restrictions are limited in scope to classified information only. Given that Meridian-nominated directors may include non-U.S. citizens, and that Meridian may seek operational integration or information-sharing in furtherance of its commercial objectives, the scope of the access restrictions in the Mitigation Agreement must be carefully calibrated to encompass both classified information and ITAR/EAR-controlled unclassified data.

**[Section 8: FOCI Mitigation Framework Overview]{.underline}**

The following is a summary of the proposed FOCI mitigation structure under the draft Mitigation Agreement (Version 3.2, dated April 18, 2025), which is being negotiated between Saxonbrook, Meridian, and CFIUS:

**Voting Trust. Meridian\'s 51% of Saxonbrook\'s outstanding common stock (5,100,000 shares) will be placed in a voting trust administered by Clearfield Trust Company. Meridian will retain economic rights only --- specifically, the right to receive dividends, distributions, and the benefit of capital appreciation upon any disposition of the shares. All voting rights will be exercised by the Voting Trustee in its sole discretion and in a manner consistent with the national security interests of the United States and the terms of the Mitigation Agreement.**

**Board Governance.** As described in Section 4 above, the post-acquisition board will consist of seven (7) members: three (3) CFIUS-approved independent U.S. citizen directors, three (3) Meridian-nominated directors (who will not hold clearances and will not have access to classified information), and one (1) management director (the CEO). The Security Committee of the Board will be composed exclusively of the CFIUS-approved independent U.S. citizen directors and will have sole oversight of all classified operations, the Government Security Director, and the Facility Security Officer.

**Government Security Director.** A GSD will be appointed with CFIUS approval and will report directly to the Security Committee. The GSD will be responsible for FOCI mitigation compliance, interface with DCSA and CFIUS, and management of the Technology Control Plan.

**Technology Control Plan (TCP).** A TCP will be developed and submitted to DCSA. The TCP will govern information barriers, IT segmentation, and access controls applicable to both classified and export-controlled information, and will detail the procedures by which classified and controlled information is safeguarded from unauthorized access.

**Third-Party Monitor.** Pinnacle Security Consultants, Inc. will serve as the Third-Party Monitor, conducting periodic compliance audits and submitting reports to CFIUS and the Security Committee.

**Information Barriers.** The Mitigation Agreement contemplates physical and electronic firewalls between classified and export-controlled operations, on the one hand, and any Meridian access points, on the other. These barriers must be designed to prevent unauthorized access to classified information and export-controlled technical data by Meridian personnel, Meridian-nominated directors, and any other foreign nationals.

The FOCI mitigation framework must be approved by both CFIUS (under the NST) and DCSA (under the NISPOM / 32 C.F.R. Part 117). The Mitigation Agreement must satisfy both sets of requirements to preserve Saxonbrook\'s FCL and its eligibility to perform on classified contracts.

                    if str(v).startswith(k): shade(cells[i], vv)
    if widths:
        for row in t.rows:
            for i,w in enumerate(widths):
                row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def gap(code, title, sev, nst, draft, analysis, fix):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(6); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    r = p.add_run(f"Gap {code} \u2014 {title} "); r.bold = True
    r2 = p.add_run(f"[{sev}]"); r2.bold = True
    r2.font.color.rgb = {"Critical":RGBColor(0xC0,0,0),"High":RGBColor(0xC5,0x5A,0x11),"Medium":RGBColor(0x7F,0x60,0x00),"Low":RGBColor(0x38,0x76,0x1D)}[sev]
    for lead, txt in (("NST: ", nst), ("Draft v3.2: ", draft), ("Analysis: ", analysis), ("Recommended fix: ", fix)):
        q = doc.add_paragraph(); q.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3); q.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
        a = q.add_run(lead); a.bold = True; q.add_run(txt)

def req_head(n, title, status, sev):
    doc.add_heading(f"Requirement {n} \u2014 {title}", level=2)
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    r = p.add_run("Overall status: "); r.bold = True
    p.add_run(status + "   ")
    r = p.add_run("Overall risk: "); r.bold = True
    p.add_run(sev)
EOF

gap("1-A","CFIUS-Approved Directors are not a majority of the Board","Critical",
 "NST 1.1–1.2: at least three CFIUS-approved independent U.S. citizen directors, who “shall comprise a majority of the Board at all times”, “irrespective of the total number of directors”. The NST gives the example directly: on a seven-member board, “a minimum of four (4) must be CFIUS-Approved Directors.”",
 "§§ 4.1–4.2 fix the Board at seven seats: 3 Independent U.S. Directors, 3 Meridian-Nominated Directors and 1 Management Director (the CEO). Exhibit A ¶ IV presents this as “4 (minimum)” U.S. citizens.",
 "3/7 = 42.9%. The NST’s own example rules out this structure. Meridian’s argument that Ms. Harlow gives a “functional” U.S. majority does not work. She is neither CFIUS-approved nor independent: she is the CEO and sits ex officio under § 4.3. Greystone conceded this in writing (Natarajan e-mail, Apr. 11). Every precedent achieved a majority of CFIUS-approved directors (A 3/5; B 4/7; C 3/5; D 5/9; E 3/5). Exhibit A’s summary row (“4 (minimum)” U.S. citizens) invites the same objection and should be deleted. The Facility Security Profile (§ 4) reaches the same conclusion.",
 "Adopt one of three structures. (a) 7 seats: 4 CFIUS-Approved / 2 Meridian / 1 Management (57.1%; Precedent B). (b) 5 seats: 3 / 1 / 1 (60%; Precedents A, C, E). (c) Our recommended compromise: 9 seats: 5 CFIUS-Approved / 3 Meridian / 1 Management (55.6%; Precedent D). Option (c) keeps the three Meridian seats that Sir Alistair calls non-negotiable and still meets NST 1.2. Whichever option is chosen, replace § 4.2 with a self-executing majority covenant: “At all times, CFIUS-Approved Directors shall constitute a majority of the directors then in office. If at any time that condition is not satisfied (including by reason of a vacancy), the Board shall not act on any matter other than filling the vacancy with a CFIUS-approved nominee, and the Meridian-Nominated Director(s) most recently appointed shall be deemed to have tendered resignation to the extent required to restore the majority.”")

 "NST 1.2 (“at all times”); NST 1.5 (vacancy filled within 60 days).",
 "§ 4.2 maintains the composition “at all times” but has no mechanism for vacancies.",
 "Even with a corrected 4/2/1 or 5/3/1 board, a single resignation among the independents (e.g., 3/6 or 4/8) leaves CFIUS-Approved Directors at or below 50% during the vacancy. Without a mechanism, Saxonbrook will be in breach every time an independent director leaves.",
 "Include the self-executing protection in Gap 1-A. Alternatively, provide for the automatic suspension of voting by one Meridian-Nominated Director during any vacancy among the CFIUS-Approved Directors.")

 "NST 1.3(c): no current employment, consulting, advisory or financial relationship with Meridian or any affiliate, subsidiary, parent or related entity, and none within the prior three years.",
 "§ 4.2(a): “no material financial, employment, or familial relationship”, with no look-back and no mention of consulting or advisory roles. Exhibit A ¶ I: “no material … relationship … within the preceding five (5) years.”",
 "The “material” qualifier lets through relationships the NST disqualifies outright. § 4.2(a) also omits consulting and advisory relationships and any look-back. The body and Exhibit A conflict (no look-back versus five years). The five-year look-back is stricter than the NST and acceptable, but the “material” qualifier is not.",

Byrd, and identify the third (or, under Option (a)/(c), the fourth and fifth) independent nominee now, because packages are due 30 days before Closing (by May 31, 2025 for a June 30 Closing).")
gap("1-E","Security Committee authority incomplete","Medium",
 "NST 1.4: “sole and exclusive authority over all matters relating to classified contracts, facility security, personnel security, export control compliance, and compliance with the Mitigation Agreement”; meetings at least quarterly; written minutes.",
 "§ 4.5: exclusive authority over “classified operations, security policies, compliance with this Agreement, and interactions with DCSA, CFIUS”; quarterly meetings; minutes.",
 "§ 4.5 does not name export control compliance, personnel security or classified contracts. Given Meridian’s stated aim of commercial cooperation on ITAR/EAR data, leaving out export control compliance matters.",
 "Restate § 4.5 using the NST 1.4 list word for word, adding “sole and” before “exclusive”. Require written minutes.")
gap("1-F","Vacancy period and DGCL removal carve-out","High",
 "NST 1.5: vacancy filled within 60 days by a CFIUS-approved replacement; removal or replacement requires CFIUS’s prior written approval.",
 "§ 4.2: the Security Committee must nominate a replacement within 45 days, with no deadline for filling the seat. § 4.4: removal requires CFIUS approval, but “[n]othing herein shall limit the statutory removal rights of shareholders under the Delaware General Corporation Law.”",
 "A deadline to nominate is not a deadline to fill. The DGCL savings clause lets the shareholders (the Voting Trustee and the 49% minority holders, including Dr. Kessler’s 22%) remove a CFIUS-Approved Director without CFIUS approval, contrary to NST 1.5. Our matrix marks this point “consistent”, which is wrong (see Part V).",
 "Require the vacancy to be filled within 60 days. Nominate within 30 days so that CFIUS has time to review. Delete the DGCL sentence, or make it subject to CFIUS’s prior written approval for any removal of a CFIUS-Approved Director. Conform the certificate of incorporation and bylaws (a Closing deliverable).")
gap("1-G","Board size frozen at seven","Low",
 "NST 1.6: the Board may expand or contract, provided the majority requirement is continuously satisfied.",
 "§ 4.1: seven members “at all times”; any change needs Security Committee consent and notice to CFIUS.",
 "This is stricter than the NST and permissible. However, it locks in the non-compliant 3/3/1 structure and would have to be amended to carry out any fix.",
 "Revise § 4.1 to fit the chosen option. Permit changes in size subject to the majority covenant, Security Committee consent and notice to CFIUS.")
gap("1-H","Meridian nomination right vs. NST 3.3(i)","Medium",
 "NST 1.6 contemplates “directors nominated by Meridian”. NST 3.3(i) provides that the Foreign Acquirer shall not be entitled to “designate, nominate, or appoint any director or observer.”",
 "§ 4.2(b) gives Meridian a contractual right to nominate three directors and to nominate replacements within 45 days. Exhibit A says Meridian nominees need not be U.S. citizens and allows no CFIUS review.",
 "The NST is internally in tension, and NST § V says the NST controls any ambiguity. CFIUS may therefore read NST 3.3(i) as limiting NST 1.6. A contractual nomination right is the most exposed form of the arrangement. Placing foreign-national directors on the board of a TS FCL contractor will also draw DCSA scrutiny.",
 "Recast § 4.2(b): Meridian may propose candidates; the Voting Trustee elects directors in its sole discretion (NST 3.2(a)); nominees are subject to Security Committee vetting and prior notice to CFIUS. Raise the point informally with Dr. Keene’s office (Kit’s planned outreach) before finalizing.")

req_head(2, "Government Security Director", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("2-A","GSD removable on notice rather than CFIUS approval","Critical",
 "NST 2.5: the GSD “shall not be removable … without the prior written approval of CFIUS”, and continues to serve pending CFIUS’s written decision.",
 "§ 5.3: removal by unanimous Security Committee vote on 30 days’ prior written notice to CFIUS, “effective upon the expiration of the thirty-day notice period.”",
 "Notice is not approval. Under the draft, the removal takes effect whether or not CFIUS objects. All five precedents require CFIUS prior written approval.",
 "Replace § 5.3 with: “The GSD may not be removed, reassigned or terminated without the prior written approval of CFIUS. Any request shall be submitted in writing with a detailed explanation, and the GSD shall continue to serve pending CFIUS’s written decision.” Add an exception permitting immediate suspension only where CFIUS or DCSA directs it.")
gap("2-B","No independent, non-reviewable access authority","Critical",
 "NST 2.4: the GSD has independent authority to deny, restrict or revoke anyone’s access (including directors and officers of Saxonbrook or Meridian) to Classified Information, Classified Spaces or Export-Controlled Technical Data. The GSD’s decisions are not subject to review, override or reversal by the Board, Meridian or anyone else other than CFIUS or the cognizant security agency.",
 "No equivalent. § 5.2 lists administrative duties only. § 8.3 visitor procedures are “approved by the Security Committee”.",
 "This is a core FOCI protection, and the draft has nothing that corresponds to it.",
 "Add a new § 5.3 (Access Authority) reproducing NST 2.4 in full, expressly covering Export-Controlled Technical Data.")
gap("2-C","Reporting line not exclusive; GSD embedded in management","High",
 "NST 2.3: the GSD reports “directly and exclusively to the Security Committee”.",
 "§ 5.1: reports directly to the Security Committee, but also “shall serve as a member of Saxonbrook’s senior management team and shall have direct access to the CEO and General Counsel”. The GSD is a “senior employee”.",
 "Placing the GSD in management makes the reporting line dual in practice. In addition, the Security Profile shows the FSO (Col. (Ret.) Delaney) reporting to the CEO and the Security Committee. The relationship between the GSD and the FSO is not addressed. Our matrix marks the reporting line “consistent”, which is wrong.",
 "Add “and exclusively”. Recast the senior-management language as access for coordination only, not a reporting relationship. Clarify that the FSO reports to the GSD on matters covered by the Agreement.")
gap("2-D","Missing Meridian look-back disqualification","High",
 "NST 2.2(d): the GSD must not be, and must not have been within the prior three years, an employee, officer, director, consultant, agent or representative of Meridian or any affiliate.",
 "§ 5.1 requires only U.S. citizenship and an active TS/SCI clearance.",
 "The independence criterion is omitted entirely.",
 "Add NST 2.2(d) to § 5.1 and to the interim-GSD qualifications in § 5.4.")
gap("2-E","Appointment timing and CFIUS approval not stated as conditions","Medium",
 "NST 2.1: appointment within 30 days of Closing. NST 2.2(c): approved in writing by CFIUS before appointment.",
 "§ 5.1: the candidate is “submitted to CFIUS for approval” 30 days before Closing. There is no appointment deadline and no express condition that CFIUS give written approval.",
 "Submitting a candidate early is helpful, but the draft never requires the GSD to be in place within 30 days after Closing, and never conditions appointment on CFIUS’s written approval.",
 "Add: “Saxonbrook shall appoint the GSD, following CFIUS’s prior written approval, no later than thirty (30) days after the Closing Date.”")
gap("2-F","Interim GSD appointed without CFIUS approval","Medium",
 "NST 2.2(c) (CFIUS approval prior to appointment) applies to the position. NST 2.5 (GSD continues to serve pending CFIUS decision).",
 "§ 5.4: Saxonbrook appoints an interim GSD within 15 business days. The permanent replacement is proposed within 45 days. The interim appointee needs no CFIUS approval and no Meridian look-back.",
 "Saxonbrook could install an unvetted interim GSD for an open-ended period.",
 "Require prompt notice of the interim appointee to CFIUS, with CFIUS able to object. Apply all of the NST 2.2 criteria to the interim appointee. Cap the interim period, or make it subject to CFIUS extension.")
gap("2-G","Responsibilities incomplete; compensation silent","Medium",
 "NST 2.3(iii): manage facility, personnel and information security and export control compliance. NST 2.6: compensation set by the Security Committee; not subject to approval, influence or review by Meridian.",
 "§ 5.2 omits management of export control compliance and “principal liaison” status, and limits the barrier duties to classified operations. There is no compensation clause.",
 "Without a compensation clause, the GSD’s pay could fall within ordinary management or Meridian-influenced budget processes.",
 "Add NST 2.3(i)–(iv) word for word, and a compensation clause tracking NST 2.6.")

req_head(3, "Voting Trust / Proxy Agreement", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("3-A","Consultation right on Fundamental Transactions","Critical",
 "NST 3.3: the Foreign Acquirer retains only economic rights and has no “governance, voting, consent, consultation, information, veto, approval, observer, or other rights”; NST 3.3(iii): no right to be consulted on decisions “beyond those directly affecting the economic value of its shareholding.”",
 "§ 6.1(c) and Ex. B ¶ 6: the Voting Trustee must consult Meridian in advance of any vote on a sale, merger, consolidation, dissolution, liquidation or change of control, and must consider Meridian’s views in good faith. § 6.2 carves this out of the Trustee’s independence (“except as contemplated by Section 6.1(c)”).",
 "“Consultation” is expressly listed as a prohibited right. A duty to consider Meridian’s views in good faith is a channel of influence over the Trustee’s vote. Greystone offered on April 15 to narrow this to notice only, but v3.2 does not reflect that offer (Rees e-mail, Apr. 17). No precedent grants such a right.",
 "Delete § 6.1(c), Ex. B ¶ 6 and the carve-out in § 6.2. As a fallback, and only with CFIUS’s concurrence, accept Greystone’s notice-only proposal. Meridian would receive written notice of a Fundamental Transaction vote no earlier than other shareholders, with no right to comment or provide input. This can be defended under the “economic value” carve-out in NST 3.3(iii), and Greystone offered it.")
gap("3-B","Board Observer right","Critical",
 "NST 3.3(i) and (iv): the Foreign Acquirer is not entitled to “designate … any director or observer” or to “attend or observe meetings of the Board or any committee thereof.”",
 "§ 6.1(d), § 8.2, Ex. B ¶ 7: Meridian designates one Board Observer who attends “all meetings” and receives all Board materials except classified or restricted materials.",
 "The NST prohibits this by name. Greystone calls the right “firm” and “standard in FOCI mitigation frameworks”. Our precedents do not support that claim: Precedent C expressly prohibits observer rights, and no precedent grants them. Even with recusal procedures, the Observer would see strategy, budgets and contract pipeline information touching classified programs. The draft also gives Meridian a seventh-seat presence on top of three nominees. (Our matrix states incorrectly that v3.2 does not extend access limits to the Observer; § 8.2 does.)",
 "Delete § 6.1(d), § 8.2, Ex. B ¶ 7, the definition of “Board Observer” and all cross-references (§§ 9.3, 15.3, 16.2; Ex. C ¶ I.C; Ex. D ¶ III(b); Ex. E § III). Meridian’s legitimate interest in information can be met through the periodic financial reporting already permitted by § 9.3, which is consistent with economic rights.")
gap("3-C","Information rights beyond economic rights","High",
 "NST 3.3: no information rights; NST 3.3(ii): no non-public information about classified operations, contracts or programs.",
 "Through the Observer, Meridian receives Board materials (§ 6.1(d)). § 9.3 allows communications on “routine unclassified corporate matters” outside GSD channels. § 13.1 provides no restriction.",
 "The materials carve-out covers only classified or Security-Committee-restricted items. Unclassified business information about classified programs (pipeline, revenue by program, rebid decisions) is still exposed.",
 "Limit Meridian’s information to (i) financial statements and dividend information provided to shareholders generally, and (ii) information needed to protect the economic value of its shares. Expressly exclude any non-public information about classified programs or contracts.")
gap("3-D","No CFIUS approval of the Voting Trustee before Closing","High",
 "NST 3.4: the Trustee must be a U.S. person with no current or prior affiliation with Meridian or its affiliates. CFIUS must approve the Trustee in writing before the Closing Date. NST § VII: naming Clearfield does not constitute approval.",
 "§§ 1.1, 6.1 name Clearfield. § 3.3(c) represents “no material business relationship”, “other than as contemplated”. CFIUS approval appears only for a successor (§ 6.4). Our matrix cites § 6.2 as providing CFIUS approval; it does not.",
 "The draft never makes CFIUS approval of Clearfield a condition. The independence representation is qualified by “material” and covers present relationships only.",
 "Add a condition: “The identity of the Voting Trustee shall have been approved in writing by CFIUS prior to the Closing Date.” Conform § 3.3(c) to “no current or prior affiliation” with Meridian or its affiliates, with no materiality qualifier.")
gap("3-E","Trust duration and modification","High",
 "NST 3.5: the Voting Arrangement remains in effect for the entire duration of Meridian’s direct or indirect ownership, and may not be terminated, modified or suspended without CFIUS’s prior written approval.",
 "Ex. B ¶ 3: the trust ends on the earlier of complete divestiture or termination of the Agreement under § 18.2. Under § 18.1, amendments require no CFIUS consent.",
 "Because § 18.1 allows the parties to amend the Agreement without CFIUS, they could also amend or end the trust without CFIUS. The draft also does not say that “ownership” includes indirect ownership.",
 "Tie the trust’s duration to Meridian’s “direct or indirect ownership interest”, and prohibit termination, modification or suspension without CFIUS’s prior written approval. The full Voting Trust Agreement (to be executed separately) must contain the same terms and should be provided to CFIUS.")
gap("3-F","No annual Trustee certification to CFIUS","High",
 "NST 3.6: the Trustee certifies to CFIUS each year, within 30 days after year-end, that the Voting Arrangement has been observed and that Meridian has exercised no unauthorized rights.",
 "§ 6.2 and Ex. B ¶ 10: quarterly reports to the Security Committee only.",
 "The NST certification is omitted.",
 "Add the certification to CFIUS, due by January 30 of each year. Keep the quarterly reports to the Security Committee.")
gap("3-G","Trustee resignation and vacancy","Medium",
 "NST 3.4–3.5 (a CFIUS-approved Trustee at all times).",
 "§ 6.4: resignation on 90 days’ notice. Saxonbrook and the Security Committee propose a successor and use “commercially reasonable efforts” to obtain CFIUS approval.",
 "A gap with no Trustee in place is possible. The 90-day resignation notice does not go to CFIUS.",
 "Provide that a resignation takes effect only when a CFIUS-approved successor accepts appointment, and that notice goes to CFIUS. Delete “commercially reasonable efforts”.")

req_head(4, "Access Restrictions", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("4-A","Export-Controlled Technical Data omitted","Critical",
 "NST 4.1(b), 4.4: no Foreign National may access Export-Controlled Technical Data (all ITAR- and EAR-controlled data, classified or not) except as specifically authorized by a valid DDTC or BIS license, license exception or other written authorization. The NST definition of “Export-Controlled Technical Data” stresses that it is broader than Classified Information.",
 "§ 8.1 restricts access only to “Classified Information or Classified Facilities”. The draft does not define Export-Controlled Technical Data. Section 15 requires general ITAR and EAR compliance and export screening, but does not impose a mitigation-agreement access restriction.",
 "Greystone confirmed in writing that the narrowing was intentional (Natarajan e-mail, Apr. 11). The exposure is concrete. The Security Profile (§ 7) states that all three programs involve ITAR-controlled data (Cat. XI(a), XII(d), IV, IV(h)), and that much of the unclassified ITAR/EAR data (drawings, test data, guidance and navigation source code) sits on a general engineering network that is not access-restricted. That network is open to about 1,160 uncleared employees. As drafted, Meridian access to that data would not breach the Agreement. All five precedents cover ITAR/EAR data. Meridian’s proposed limitation to data “arising from or related to” classified programs is also inconsistent with NST 4.4 (“whether or not such information is also classified”).",
 "Adopt the NST definition of Export-Controlled Technical Data and add new § 8.1(b) (Rees proposal, Apr. 16), extended to cover all three NST categories: “No Foreign National … shall have access to (a) Classified Information, (b) Export-Controlled Technical Data held by or generated by Saxonbrook, or (c) Classified Spaces, without prior written authorization from the appropriate United States Government agency … Access to Export-Controlled Technical Data is prohibited except as specifically authorized by a valid export license, license exception, or other written authorization issued by DDTC or BIS.” Negotiating point: NST 4.4 already gives Meridian a route to legitimate commercial synergies. Meridian can apply for transaction-specific DDTC or BIS authorizations for Saxonbrook data, documented and logged by the GSD. That answers Greystone’s objection that the restriction would “prevent all commercial cooperation”. Meridian’s existing TAAs cover its own programs for BAE Systems, not Saxonbrook’s data.")
gap("4-B","“Foreign National” definition excludes LPRs and foreign entities","Critical",
 "NST § IV: “Foreign National” means any individual who is not a U.S. citizen or U.S. national, and any non-U.S.-organized entity or other foreign person under 31 C.F.R. § 800.224.",
 "§ 1.1: any individual who is not a U.S. citizen “or a United States lawful permanent resident”. Entities are not covered.",
 "This narrowing has not been raised in the negotiations. It carries the ITAR “U.S. person” concept, under which LPRs are U.S. persons, into a CFIUS instrument that is deliberately stricter. As drafted, a Meridian employee who holds a U.S. green card would fall outside every Foreign National restriction in §§ 8, 9.3, 15.3 and 16.1(f). Meridian entities themselves would also fall outside those restrictions.",
 "Adopt the NST definition word for word.")
gap("4-C","Reliance on international security agreements and foreign clearances","High",
 "NST 4.2: the restriction applies “regardless of the nationality … regardless of any security clearance … issued by a foreign government, and regardless of whether any bilateral security agreement or industrial security arrangement exists.”",
 "§ 8.1: access is permitted on authorization “in accordance with … the terms of any applicable international security agreement.”",
 "This conflicts directly with NST 4.2. Given Meridian’s reliance on the U.S.–UK Defense Trade Cooperation Treaty and its UK clearances, the clause is a likely route to UK-cleared Meridian personnel gaining access.",
 "Delete the international-agreement wording and insert NST 4.2 word for word. Also make clear that no ITAR exemption (e.g., 22 C.F.R. § 126.17 treaty exemption) may be relied on for access by Meridian personnel to Saxonbrook data unless the GSD has documented it and notified CFIUS in advance.")
gap("4-D","Enforcement controls incomplete","Medium",
 "NST 4.3: visitor management, mandatory escorts for all non-cleared personnel in proximity to classified areas, electronic access control lists, regular audits of access logs.",
 "§ 8.3 and Ex. C: sign-in, badges, escorts for Foreign National visitors only, a visit log, and monthly log review (Ex. C ¶ IV).",
 "There is no escort requirement for non-cleared U.S. persons near classified areas, and no controls over export-controlled areas or systems. § 8.3 (Foreign Nationals “prohibited from entering classified areas”) also conflicts with § 8.1 (entry possible with authorization).",
 "Insert the NST 4.3 controls, applying them to both classified areas and export-controlled areas and systems. Reconcile §§ 8.1 and 8.3.")

req_head(5, "Information Barriers", "Partially compliant", "High")
gap("5-A","Barriers limited to classified operations","High",
 "NST 5.1: barriers between Saxonbrook’s “classified and export-controlled operations” and Meridian, to prevent disclosure of Classified Information or Export-Controlled Technical Data.",
 "§ 9.1: physical barriers between “classified operations” and Meridian. § 9.2(a)–(b): electronic separation of “classified” IT systems. § 9.2(c) covers only “sensitive but unclassified information” (an undefined term).",
 "This is the same scope defect as Gap 4-A, in the barrier provisions. NST 5.2(a)–(c) and 5.3(a) each expressly cover export-controlled areas, materials and systems.",
 "Extend §§ 9.1 and 9.2 to “classified and export-controlled operations, areas, materials and systems”. Require the general engineering network holding ITAR/EAR data to be segmented from any system accessible to Meridian before Closing.")
gap("5-B","Shared-infrastructure prohibition incomplete","High",
 "NST 5.3(b): no shared IT infrastructure, including email servers, cloud platforms, ERP systems, data analytics tools and collaborative software, between classified or export-controlled operations and Meridian.",
 "§ 9.2(a) separates classified systems from “Meridian-connected networks” (intranet, email, file-sharing). There is no reference to ERP, analytics or collaboration tools, and no reference to export-controlled operations. Ex. C ¶ II.D addresses classified data on cloud platforms only.",
 "Post-closing integration of ERP and financial systems is a common source of leakage of export-controlled data.",
 "Insert the NST 5.3(b) list word for word, applying it to classified and export-controlled operations.")
gap("5-C","Monitoring controls","Medium",
 "NST 5.3(c): intrusion detection, data loss prevention and continuous monitoring on all network boundaries.",
 "§ 9.2(c) and Ex. C ¶ II.C: DLP on unclassified email. The intrusion detection systems in § 9.2 are physical-security upgrades.",
 "Network intrusion detection and continuous monitoring on all boundaries are not required.",
 "Add NST 5.3(c) word for word.")
gap("5-D","No exception mechanism (GSD sole authority plus CFIUS prior approval)","Medium",
 "NST 5.4: only the GSD may approve exceptions, and only with CFIUS’s prior written approval.",
 "None. Ex. C ¶ II.B (removable media) requires GSD authorization only.",
 "Without the provision, exceptions could be granted by management or the Board.",
 "Add NST 5.4.")
gap("5-E","120-day implementation window for physical upgrades","Medium",
 "NST 5.1 requires Saxonbrook to “establish and maintain” barriers. Access restrictions apply “at all times following the Closing.” The NST sets no phase-in period.",
 "§ 9.2 (final paragraph): physical upgrades (controlled-access barriers, badge readers, intrusion detection) completed within 120 days of Closing.",
 "Our matrix says the NST requires barriers to be “fully operational prior to closing”. The NST does not say this expressly (see Part V), so the point should not be argued in those terms. Even so, a 120-day period after Closing in which barriers are incomplete, during which Meridian obtains its 51% interest, is inconsistent with the barriers being maintained from Closing. Four of five precedents required barriers before closing.",
 "Require the barriers sufficient to enforce Requirements 4 and 5 (including segmentation of the engineering network) to be in place at Closing, certified by the GSD. Only incremental hardening may be completed within a short period afterwards, and any such schedule should be disclosed to CFIUS. Separately, the “total estimated annual compliance cost” of $1,200,000 mixes one-time capital upgrades with recurring costs and should be relabeled.")

req_head(6, "Personnel Vetting", "Partially compliant", "High")
gap("6-A","CFIUS removal: 30 days and no immediate exclusion","High",
 "NST 6.2: removal within 10 business days of CFIUS notice; the individual is immediately excluded from all classified and export-controlled work areas pending removal.",
 "§ 7.2: compliance within 30 days of notice. No interim exclusion.",
 "The draft triples the period, and a person CFIUS has found to be a risk could keep access for a month. Our matrix marks Requirement 6 “consistent”, which is wrong.",
 "Conform to 10 business days, with immediate exclusion upon receipt of notice.")
gap("6-B","Enhanced investigations not DCSA-directed; scope omits export-controlled access and future access","Medium",
 "NST 6.1: enhanced background investigations “as directed by DCSA, at Saxonbrook’s expense”, for directors, officers and employees who “have or will have access” to Classified Information or Export-Controlled Technical Data.",
 "§ 7.1: conducted “by or at the direction of the Government Security Director”. Covers only those who “have access to Classified Programs or Classified Information”. No reference to cost.",
 "The draft changes who directs the investigations, leaves out export-controlled access and future access, and is silent on cost.",
 "Conform to NST 6.1.")
gap("6-C","No pre-duty vetting of new hires/transferees","Medium",
 "NST 6.3: new hires and transferees must be vetted and cleared before beginning classified or export-controlled duties.",
 "None.",
 "The requirement is omitted.",
 "Add NST 6.3.")
gap("6-D","No clearance roster obligation","Low",
 "NST 6.4: a current roster (clearance level, date of issuance, program access), provided to DCSA and CFIUS on request.",
 "§ 7.4 states the clearance population and requires adverse-action reporting. There is no roster.",
 "The requirement is omitted.",
 "Add NST 6.4.")

req_head(7, "Technology Control Plan", "Partially compliant", "High")
gap("7-A","Deadline measured from wrong trigger and wrong period","High",
 "NST 7.2: the TCP is developed within 60 days of the Closing Date and submitted to DCSA for review and approval.",
 "§ 9.4: submitted to DCSA “within ninety (90) days of the Effective Date”, where the Effective Date is CFIUS clearance (§ 1.1).",
 "On the current timetable (clearance about May 15; Closing June 30), v3.2 produces August 13, 2025, which is earlier than the NST date of August 29, 2025 (also shown in the Security Profile). The two clocks diverge whenever clearance and Closing are less than 30 days apart. In the limiting case (clearance and Closing on the same day), v3.2 would allow 90 days against the NST’s 60. CFIUS will expect its own formulation. The NST metric is 60 days from Closing in four of five precedents.",
 "“within the earlier of sixty (60) days after the Closing Date or ninety (90) days after the Effective Date”, or simply track NST 7.2. Begin drafting the TCP now, because the Security Profile already identifies the engineering-network issue.")
gap("7-B","Required contents missing","Medium",
 "NST 7.3(a)–(g): includes (c) insider threat detection, (d) visitor access procedures (escorted and unescorted), (e) handling, storage, transmission, reproduction and destruction of ITAR- and EAR-controlled materials, and (g) security incident reporting procedures.",
 "§ 9.5(a)–(g): classified-material handling, electronic and physical security, personnel protocols, training, incident response, and audit. No insider-threat component, no visitor procedures, and no detailed ITAR/EAR handling (§ 9.4 refers generally to “handling of export-controlled materials”).",
 "Several NST content items are missing.",
 "Insert NST 7.3(a)–(g) as the minimum content. Keep v3.2’s additional training and audit items.")
gap("7-C","No annual update; GSD responsibility","Medium",
 "NST 7.4: reviewed and updated at least annually, or more often as DCSA or CFIUS requires or circumstances warrant. NST 7.5: the GSD is responsible for developing, implementing and enforcing the TCP.",
 "§ 9.4: “periodic review and update as necessary”. § 5.2(a): the GSD oversees compliance with the TCP.",
 "The draft has no minimum review frequency, and the GSD is not made responsible for developing the TCP.",
 "Add an annual minimum review, triggers for event-driven updates, and NST 7.5.")

doc.add_heading("IV. Requirement-by-Requirement Analysis", level=1)

req_head(1, "Board Composition", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("1-A","CFIUS-Approved Directors are not a majority of the Board","Critical",
 "NST 1.1\u20131.2: at least three CFIUS-approved independent U.S. citizen directors, who \u201cshall comprise a majority of the Board at all times\u201d, \u201cirrespective of the total number of directors\u201d. The NST gives the example directly: on a seven-member board, \u201ca minimum of four (4) must be CFIUS-Approved Directors.\u201d",
 "\u00a7\u00a7 4.1\u20134.2 fix the Board at seven seats: 3 Independent U.S. Directors, 3 Meridian-Nominated Directors and 1 Management Director (the CEO). Exhibit A \u00b6 IV presents this as \u201c4 (minimum)\u201d U.S. citizens.",
 "3/7 = 42.9%. The NST\u2019s own example rules out this structure. Meridian\u2019s argument that Ms. Harlow gives a \u201cfunctional\u201d U.S. majority does not work. She is neither CFIUS-approved nor independent: she is the CEO and sits ex officio under \u00a7 4.3. Greystone conceded this in writing (Natarajan e-mail, Apr. 11). Every precedent achieved a majority of CFIUS-approved directors (A 3/5; B 4/7; C 3/5; D 5/9; E 3/5). Exhibit A\u2019s summary row (\u201c4 (minimum)\u201d U.S. citizens) invites the same objection and should be deleted. The Facility Security Profile (\u00a7 4) reaches the same conclusion.",
 "Adopt one of three structures. (a) 7 seats: 4 CFIUS-Approved / 2 Meridian / 1 Management (57.1%; Precedent B). (b) 5 seats: 3 / 1 / 1 (60%; Precedents A, C, E). (c) Our recommended compromise: 9 seats: 5 CFIUS-Approved / 3 Meridian / 1 Management (55.6%; Precedent D). Option (c) keeps the three Meridian seats that Sir Alistair calls non-negotiable and still meets NST 1.2. Whichever option is chosen, replace \u00a7 4.2 with a self-executing majority covenant: \u201cAt all times, CFIUS-Approved Directors shall constitute a majority of the directors then in office. If at any time that condition is not satisfied (including by reason of a vacancy), the Board shall not act on any matter other than filling the vacancy with a CFIUS-approved nominee, and the Meridian-Nominated Director(s) most recently appointed shall be deemed to have tendered resignation to the extent required to restore the majority.\u201d")

gap("6-B","Enhanced investigations not DCSA-directed; scope omits export-controlled access and future access","Medium",

 "\u00a7 7.1: conducted \u201cby or at the direction of the Government Security Director\u201d. Covers only those who \u201chave access to Classified Programs or Classified Information\u201d. No reference to cost.",
 "The draft changes who directs the investigations, leaves out export-controlled access and future access, and is silent on cost.",
 "Conform to NST 6.1.")
gap("6-C","No pre-duty vetting of new hires/transferees","Medium",
 "NST 6.3: new hires and transferees must be vetted and cleared before beginning classified or export-controlled duties.",
 "None.",
 "The requirement is omitted.",
 "Add NST 6.3.")
gap("6-D","No clearance roster obligation","Low",
 "NST 6.4: a current roster (clearance level, date of issuance, program access), provided to DCSA and CFIUS on request.",
 "\u00a7 7.4 states the clearance population and requires adverse-action reporting. There is no roster.",
 "The requirement is omitted.",
 "Add NST 6.4.")

req_head(7, "Technology Control Plan", "Partially compliant", "High")
gap("7-A","Deadline measured from wrong trigger and wrong period","High",
 "NST 7.2: the TCP is developed within 60 days of the Closing Date and submitted to DCSA for review and approval.",
 "\u00a7 9.4: submitted to DCSA \u201cwithin ninety (90) days of the Effective Date\u201d, where the Effective Date is CFIUS clearance (\u00a7 1.1).",
 "On the current timetable (clearance about May 15; Closing June 30), v3.2 produces August 13, 2025, which is earlier than the NST date of August 29, 2025 (also shown in the Security Profile). The two clocks diverge whenever clearance and Closing are less than 30 days apart. In the limiting case (clearance and Closing on the same day), v3.2 would allow 90 days against the NST\u2019s 60. CFIUS will expect its own formulation. The NST metric is 60 days from Closing in four of five precedents.",
 "\u201cwithin the earlier of sixty (60) days after the Closing Date or ninety (90) days after the Effective Date\u201d, or simply track NST 7.2. Begin drafting the TCP now, because the Security Profile already identifies the engineering-network issue.")
gap("7-B","Required contents missing","Medium",
 "NST 7.3(a)\u2013(g): includes (c) insider threat detection, (d) visitor access procedures (escorted and unescorted), (e) handling, storage, transmission, reproduction and destruction of ITAR- and EAR-controlled materials, and (g) security incident reporting procedures.",
 "\u00a7 9.5(a)\u2013(g): classified-material handling, electronic and physical security, personnel protocols, training, incident response, and audit. No insider-threat component, no visitor procedures, and no detailed ITAR/EAR handling (\u00a7 9.4 refers generally to \u201chandling of export-controlled materials\u201d).",
 "Several NST content items are missing.",
 "Insert NST 7.3(a)\u2013(g) as the minimum content. Keep v3.2\u2019s additional training and audit items.")
gap("7-C","No annual update; GSD responsibility","Medium",
 "NST 7.4: reviewed and updated at least annually, or more often as DCSA or CFIUS requires or circumstances warrant. NST 7.5: the GSD is responsible for developing, implementing and enforcing the TCP.",
 "\u00a7 9.4: \u201cperiodic review and update as necessary\u201d. \u00a7 5.2(a): the GSD oversees compliance with the TCP.",
 "The draft has no minimum review frequency, and the GSD is not made responsible for developing the TCP.",
 "Add an annual minimum review, triggers for event-driven updates, and NST 7.5.")

req_head(8, "Third-Party Monitor", "Non-compliant", "High")
gap("8-A","Annual rather than semiannual audits","High",
 "NST 8.3: semiannual compliance audits (every six months).",
 "§ 12.1 and Ex. D ¶ V: annual audits. The first audit is due within 12 months of Closing.",
 "The draft halves the required frequency, and the first audit could come almost a year after Closing. Four of five precedents are semiannual; only Precedent E (2024, Australia) is annual. Meridian is likely to cite Precedent E, but the NST’s express term controls.",
 "Require audits every six months, the first within six months of Closing. The cost effect (Pinnacle’s $475,000 fee, payable by Saxonbrook) should be repriced with Pinnacle now.")
gap("8-B","No report delivery deadline","High",
 "NST 8.4: written reports to CFIUS within 30 days of completion of each audit.",
 "§ 12.2 and Ex. D ¶ VI: reports to the Security Committee and CFIUS, with no deadline.",
 "The draft contains no deadline at all. All precedents set 30 days, except Precedent D (21 days).",
 "Add “within thirty (30) days after completion of each audit”.")
gap("8-C","No CFIUS approval of the Monitor; no CFIUS replacement right","High",
 "NST 8.1: the Monitor must be approved by CFIUS. NST 8.7: CFIUS may require replacement at any time, and the parties must engage a CFIUS-approved successor within 30 days. NST § VII: naming Pinnacle does not constitute approval.",
 "§ 1.1 defines the Monitor as Pinnacle. No provision conditions the appointment on CFIUS approval or gives CFIUS a replacement right. Our matrix states that § 12.4 requires CFIUS approval; § 12.4 is the fee clause.",
 "The NST approval and replacement mechanism is missing.",
 "Add CFIUS written approval as a condition precedent, the NST 8.7 replacement right, and a 30-day successor obligation.")
gap("8-D","Independence qualifiers; fee set by Saxonbrook and Monitor","Medium",
 "NST 8.2: no affiliation, financial interest or business relationship with either Saxonbrook or Meridian or their affiliates.",
 "§ 3.4(c): no “material” financial interest or business relationship. Ex. D ¶ VII is similar. § 12.4: the fee is “adjusted by mutual agreement of Saxonbrook and the Third-Party Monitor.”",
 "The materiality qualifier weakens the NST test. Annual fee negotiations between the Monitor and the audited company create a structural incentive that CFIUS may question. Cost allocation itself is left to the parties (NST 8.6), so payment by Saxonbrook is permissible.",
 "Delete “material”. Provide that fee adjustments are approved by the Security Committee and disclosed to CFIUS, and that fees may not be reduced while an audit is open.")
gap("8-E","Audit scope and report contents incomplete; GSD not copied","Medium",
 "NST 8.3 scope includes “the GSD’s activities and independence” and “subcontracting compliance”. NST 8.4(a)–(e) report contents include scope and methodology and an assessment of overall effectiveness. NST 8.5: copies go to the Security Committee and the GSD at the same time as to CFIUS.",
 "§ 12.1 and Ex. D ¶ III omit GSD independence and subcontracting. The report contents do not expressly require scope and methodology. § 12.2 sends copies to the Security Committee and CFIUS only.",
 "Several NST scope, content and distribution items are missing.",
 "Add the missing scope items and NST 8.4(a)–(e) contents, and distribute copies at the same time to CFIUS, the Security Committee and the GSD. Keep v3.2’s compliance ratings and trend comparison, which exceed the NST.")

req_head(9, "Annual Compliance Report", "Non-compliant", "High")
gap("9-A","Deadline extendable by the Monitor","High",
 "NST 9.2: no later than March 31 each year. The date is fixed and may not be extended “by the parties, the Third-Party Monitor, or any other person” without CFIUS’s prior written approval.",
 "§ 12.3 and Ex. E: “within ninety (90) days following the end of each calendar year, or such later date as agreed by the Third-Party Monitor.”",
 "The extension mechanism is expressly prohibited. Separately, 90 days does not always equal March 31: in leap years (e.g., 2028) it falls on March 30. It is better to use the NST date. All five precedents use a fixed March 31.",
 "“no later than March 31 of each year; this deadline may not be extended except with the prior written approval of CFIUS.”")
gap("9-B","Certifications and signatories wrong","High",
 "NST 9.3(a): a certification by the GSD and the Chair of the Security Committee of material compliance with the Mitigation Agreement. NST 9.4: signed by the CEO and the GSD, certifying accuracy and completeness.",
 "§ 12.3(b): a GSD certification limited to TCP compliance. § 12.3(f): a certification by the CEO and General Counsel. Ex. E signature blocks: CEO and GSD.",
 "The scope of certification is narrower than the NST requires. The Security Committee Chair is omitted. § 12.3(f) is internally inconsistent with Exhibit E.",
 "Conform to NST 9.3(a) and 9.4, and conform Exhibit E. The General Counsel may be added as an additional signatory.")
gap("9-C","Required contents missing","Medium",
 "NST 9.3(d): organizational chart (Board, Security Committee, GSD). NST 9.3(e): changes to classified contracts. NST 9.3(f): financial information on viability, including revenue for classified and unclassified operations. NST 9.3(g): other information CFIUS requests.",
 "§ 12.3(a)–(f) omits the organizational chart and item (g). Financial content is limited to statements certified by Ashford & Lyle “to the extent relevant to compliance costs”. Exhibit E covers contract status, but the body does not require it.",
 "CFIUS uses the viability financials to monitor dependence on classified revenue (64.3% of FY2024 revenue). Limiting financial content to compliance costs does not meet NST 9.3(f).",
 "Add NST 9.3(d)–(g) to § 12.3, and add organizational chart and viability-financials sections to Exhibit E.")
gap("9-D","No stub-period first report","Low",
 "NST 9.5: the first report covers the Closing Date through December 31 of the year of Closing.",
 "Not addressed.",
 "On a June 30, 2025 Closing, the first report (covering July 1 to December 31, 2025) is due March 31, 2026.",
 "Add NST 9.5.")

req_head(10, "Incident Reporting", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("10-A","72 hours from GSD determination rather than 24 hours from discovery","Critical",
 "NST 10.1: report within 24 hours of discovery. NST 10.2: “discovery” occurs when any Saxonbrook employee, officer, director, agent, contractor or representative first becomes aware of facts reasonably indicating a breach, and the obligation “shall not be conditioned upon or delayed pending investigation, verification, or determination by the GSD.” NST 10.4: the clock “commences upon discovery by any Saxonbrook personnel” and does not depend on the GSD’s awareness.",
 "§ 14.2: within 72 hours after the GSD “determines that a Reportable Incident has occurred.” The GSD makes that determination “as promptly as practicable”, and the clock runs only from the GSD’s “affirmative determination.”",
 "The draft triples the reporting window. It also makes the start of the clock open-ended and dependent on the GSD’s determination, which is the gatekeeping step the NST forbids. All five precedents use 24 hours from discovery. Kit Holloway’s view is that CFIUS has not, to our knowledge, accepted anything longer. Meridian’s concern about unverified “noise” is already answered by the NST: the initial report may be preliminary and limited to facts “to the extent known”, may be sent by e-mail (NST 10.3), and is followed by a detailed report. The obligation is therefore not “duplicative”; the NST itself requires it.",
 "Replace § 14.2 with NST 10.1–10.4: a preliminary written report (e-mail acceptable) to Dr. Keene within 24 hours of discovery by any Saxonbrook personnel, and a detailed follow-up within five business days. Jonathan’s proposed 72-hour supplemental report may be added as an intermediate update, but it cannot replace the 24-hour notice and must not lengthen the five-business-day follow-up. Add an internal duty requiring all personnel to escalate immediately to the GSD, and cover it in training under § 16.1(e).")
gap("10-B","Follow-up report and contents","Medium",
 "NST 10.3: the initial report includes a preliminary description, the date and time of discovery and the persons involved. A detailed written follow-up is due within five business days.",
 "§ 14.3 sets out a single, detailed report (contents (a)–(g)). There is no two-stage structure.",
 "§ 14.3’s content list is good, but it should apply to the follow-up report.",
 "Two-stage structure: initial report (NST 10.3 contents) and follow-up report (the § 14.3 contents).")
gap("10-C","Parallel reporting incomplete; scope cross-check","Low",
 "NST 10.5: parallel reporting to DCSA, the cognizant security agency, the relevant contracting officer and other U.S. Government agencies. NST 10.1 covers any actual or suspected breach, including unauthorized access to Export-Controlled Technical Data or Classified Spaces.",
 "§ 14.2: DCSA “to the extent required by applicable NISPOM provisions”. § 14.1(a) covers only classified information and facilities.",
 "Contracting officers and other agencies (e.g., DDTC voluntary disclosures) are not referenced. § 14.1(a) should also cover access to export-controlled data, although § 14.1(c)–(d) catch most of it.",
 "Add NST 10.5, and extend § 14.1(a) to Export-Controlled Technical Data and Classified Spaces.")

req_head(11, "Government Contracts Continuity", "Non-compliant", "High")
gap("11-A","Notice period, recipient and triggers","High",
 "NST 11.2: 90 days’ prior written notice delivered directly to the CFIUS monitoring contact of any decision to terminate, not rebid, or materially reduce the scope of a classified contract, with detailed reasons, impact and continuity steps.",
 "§ 10.2: 60 days’ notice to the Security Committee, which “shall promptly inform CFIUS”. The triggers are termination, non-renewal and non-rebid only.",
 "The draft shortens the period by 30 days and routes notice through an intermediary, so CFIUS could receive materially less than 60 days. Material reductions in scope are omitted. Four of five precedents use 90 days direct to CFIUS; only Precedent D used 60.",
 "Conform to NST 11.2: 90 days, direct to Dr. Keene, with a copy to the Security Committee, and include material scope reductions.")
gap("11-B","No CFIUS direction right during notice period","Medium",
 "NST 11.3: during the notice period, CFIUS may consult the contracting agencies and direct the steps necessary for continuity of supply and protection of classified information.",
 "None.",
 "The CFIUS direction right is omitted.",
 "Add NST 11.3.")
gap("11-C","No obligation to rebid or to consult before declining","High",
 "NST 11.4: commercially reasonable efforts to rebid and retain classified contracts. NST 11.5: Saxonbrook must consult CFIUS before declining to rebid.",
 "§ 10.1 requires commercially reasonable efforts to continue performance of existing contracts. There is no rebid covenant and no consultation duty. Our matrix states that § 10.1 contains an “affirmative obligation to pursue rebid”; it does not.",
 "Both NST obligations are omitted. On the current timetable this matters: all three programs ($312.0M) will in time come up for recompetition.",
 "Add NST 11.4 and 11.5. Make clear that the “commercially unreasonable terms” exception in NST 11.5 is available only after consultation with CFIUS.")
gap("11-D","Absolute maintenance covenant qualified","Low",
 "NST 11.1: maintain all existing classified contracts “without interruption”.",
 "§ 10.1 states the covenant but adds “commercially reasonable efforts to continue performance”.",
 "The efforts qualifier could be read to soften the unqualified maintenance obligation.",
 "Make the efforts language an additional obligation (“and shall use”), not a qualifier.")
gap("11-E","New-contract notification","Low",
 "NST App. A: prompt notice to CFIUS and DCSA of new classified awards, modifications, extensions or terminations.",
 "§ 10.3: notice to the Security Committee and GSD within 30 days, and only where the award “materially alter[s]” security posture. § 13.1(e): “prompt” notice to CFIUS of new awards and material modifications (value change greater than 10%). DCSA is not covered.",
 "§§ 10.3 and 13.1(e) are inconsistent with each other, and DCSA notice is omitted.",
 "Harmonize: prompt notice to CFIUS and DCSA of every new award, modification, extension or termination.")

req_head(12, "Subcontracting Restrictions", "Non-compliant", "High")
gap("12-A","25% direct-equity threshold rather than 10% direct or indirect","High",
 "NST 12.1: no subcontracting of classified work, without CFIUS’s prior written approval, to any Meridian affiliate or any entity in which Meridian holds a 10% or greater interest, “whether such interest is held directly or indirectly, including through subsidiaries, affiliates, joint ventures, partnerships, or other arrangements.”",
 "§ 11.3: 25% or greater “direct equity interest”, measured “as reflected on Meridian’s books and records.” § 11.2: an absolute bar on Meridian and its subsidiaries, affiliates and parent. “Affiliate” is undefined.",
 "Greystone acknowledged that the 25% threshold was “specifically calibrated” to exclude Meridian joint ventures in France, Germany, Japan and South Korea in which it holds 10–24% (Rees e-mail, Apr. 17). Those are the entities the NST is aimed at. The “direct” qualifier excludes the joint-venture and consortium structures that NST 12.1 names. Measuring by Meridian’s own books and records leaves Meridian to determine whether the test is met. All five precedents use 10%, and two expressly include indirect interests. The absolute bar in § 11.2 exceeds the NST and is acceptable, but because “affiliate” is undefined it cannot fill the gap.",
 "Conform to NST 12.1 (10%, direct or indirect). Answer the diligence-burden concern by requiring Meridian to deliver at signing, and update quarterly, a certified schedule of every entity in which it holds a direct or indirect interest of 10% or more. This puts the diligence burden on Meridian, which holds the information. Note that the NST requires prior CFIUS approval, not a ban. Approval requests for specific joint-venture subcontractors can be made case by case.")
gap("12-B","No lower-tier flow-down","High",
 "NST 12.2: the restriction applies at all tiers, and subcontractors must be contractually bound not to subcontract further to restricted entities without CFIUS approval.",
 "None.",
 "Without flow-down, classified work could reach a 10%-plus Meridian joint venture at the second tier.",
 "Add NST 12.2 and a mandatory flow-down clause.")
gap("12-C","“Classified work” undefined; list omits country of organization","Low",
 "NST 12.3 defines “classified work”. NST 12.4: the subcontractor list includes country of organization and is available to CFIUS and the Monitor.",
 "No definition. § 11.4 lists name, address, ownership and work description, updated quarterly.",
 "These are minor conforming points. The quarterly update is stricter than the NST and acceptable.",
 "Add the NST 12.3 definition and country of organization.")

req_head(13, "Amendment and Termination", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("13-A","Amendments without CFIUS consent","Critical",
 "NST 13.1: amendment only with the prior written consent of all parties and CFIUS. No amendment, modification, waiver or supplement is effective unless signed by all parties and approved in writing by CFIUS. Waivers require CFIUS’s express written consent.",
 "§ 18.1: a written instrument signed by Saxonbrook, Meridian and the Voting Trustee. CFIUS is omitted, and so is Pinnacle, although it is a Party. § 18.9: a waiver is effective if signed “by the Party granting such waiver”.",
 "As drafted, the private parties could unilaterally amend or waive any mitigation term, including the voting trust. All precedents require CFIUS consent.",
 "Replace § 18.1 and § 18.9 with NST 13.1 word for word, covering all Parties and CFIUS.")
gap("13-B","Automatic termination with fixed 12-month wind-down","Critical",
 "NST 13.2: in force for the duration of Meridian’s direct or indirect ownership, and does not lapse through the passage of time alone. NST 13.3: may survive divestiture at CFIUS’s “sole and unreviewable discretion”, including indefinitely. NST 13.4: termination only by petition to CFIUS, which may refuse or impose conditions.",
 "§ 18.2: terminates “automatically upon the complete divestiture”. Sections 8, 9, 12 and 14 survive for 12 months only, then “all obligations … shall cease.” Ex. D ¶ II and Ex. B ¶ 3 are tied to this mechanism.",
 "The fixed wind-down replaces CFIUS’s discretion with a contractual end date. Divestiture to another foreign buyer, or a partial divestiture through indirect structures, could end the protections. “Ownership interest” is not stated to include indirect ownership. There is no petition mechanism. All precedents preserve CFIUS’s discretion over survival.",
 "Replace § 18.2 with NST 13.2–13.4. Any wind-down period may be expressed only as a minimum survival period, subject to CFIUS’s determination.")
gap("13-C","Evidence-preservation survival and other survival clauses","Low",
 "NST 13.3 (CFIUS determines survival).",
 "§ 14.4: evidence is preserved for 5 years and survives termination.",
 "This is consistent with the NST and exceeds it. It should be preserved in the revised survival clause.",
 "Cross-reference in the revised § 18.2.")

req_head(14, "Penalties and Enforcement", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("14-A","Penalty capped at $250,000; transaction-value measure omitted","Critical",
 "NST 14.1: civil penalties of up to $250,000 per violation or the value of the transaction, “whichever is greater”. The transaction value is $588,285,000.",
 "§ 17.1: penalties “not to exceed Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($250,000) per violation.”",
 "The draft turns a minimum into a cap and removes an alternative measure of more than $588 million. CFIUS will not accept a contractual limit on its own penalty authority (NST 14.6–14.7). In addition, we understand that CFIUS’s November 2024 amendments to its penalty regulations (31 C.F.R. § 800.901, effective December 2024) raised the per-violation maximum for breaches of mitigation agreements above the $250,000 figure stated in the NST. That should be confirmed before submission. Either way, a hard dollar cap in the Agreement is inadvisable.",
 "Track NST 14.1, and add “or such greater amount as may be provided under 50 U.S.C. § 4565 and 31 C.F.R. Part 800 as in effect from time to time.”")
gap("14-B","Continuing violations not treated as separate per-day violations","High",
 "NST 14.2: each day a violation continues is a separate violation.",
 "None.",
 "Read together with the 30-day cure period (Gap 14-D), the omission substantially reduces exposure for continuing breaches.",
 "Add NST 14.2.")
gap("14-C","Forced divestiture and Presidential authority omitted","Critical",
 "NST 14.4: potential forced divestiture under 50 U.S.C. § 4565(d)(4), with the parties’ acknowledgment. NST 14.5: Presidential authority over classified contracts and FCLs. NST 14.6: remedies are cumulative.",
 "§ 17.1 refers to injunctive relief and DOJ referral. § 17.3 preserves authority “including … suspending or prohibiting the Transaction”. Divestiture is not mentioned.",
 "Every precedent includes forced divestiture. Leaving out the parties’ express acknowledgment will be read as deliberate.",
 "Insert NST 14.3–14.7 word for word, including Meridian’s acknowledgment of the divestiture authority.")
gap("14-D","New 30-day cure period","High",
 "No cure period in the NST. Remedies are cumulative and CFIUS’s authority “is not limited, constrained, or waived” (NST 14.6–14.7).",
 "§ 17.2: 30 days to cure after CFIUS notice. Only a failure to cure “shall constitute a material breach.”",
 "The negative implication is that an uncured violation is not a material breach until 30 days have passed. That sits uneasily with per-violation penalties and per-day accrual, and limits CFIUS’s remedies.",
 "Delete § 17.2. As a fallback, recast it as a discretionary cure that CFIUS may grant, stating expressly that it does not limit penalties, per-day accrual or any other remedy.")
EOF
echo ok'

req_head(9, "Annual Compliance Report", "Non-compliant", "High")
gap("9-A","Deadline extendable by the Monitor","High",
 "NST 9.2: no later than March 31 each year. The date is fixed and may not be extended \u201cby the parties, the Third-Party Monitor, or any other person\u201d without CFIUS\u2019s prior written approval.",
 "\u00a7 12.3 and Ex. E: \u201cwithin ninety (90) days following the end of each calendar year, or such later date as agreed by the Third-Party Monitor.\u201d",
