gap("9-B","Certifications and signatories wrong","High",
 "NST 9.3(a): a certification by the GSD and the Chair of the Security Committee of material compliance with the Mitigation Agreement. NST 9.4: signed by the CEO and the GSD, certifying accuracy and completeness.",
 "\u00a7 12.3(b): a GSD certification limited to TCP compliance. \u00a7 12.3(f): a certification by the CEO and General Counsel. Ex. E signature blocks: CEO and GSD.",
 "The scope of certification is narrower than the NST requires. The Security Committee Chair is omitted. \u00a7 12.3(f) is internally inconsistent with Exhibit E.",
 "Conform to NST 9.3(a) and 9.4, and conform Exhibit E. The General Counsel may be added as an additional signatory.")
gap("9-C","Required contents missing","Medium",
 "NST 9.3(d): organizational chart (Board, Security Committee, GSD). NST 9.3(e): changes to classified contracts. NST 9.3(f): financial information on viability, including revenue for classified and unclassified operations. NST 9.3(g): other information CFIUS requests.",
 "\u00a7 12.3(a)\u2013(f) omits the organizational chart and item (g). Financial content is limited to statements certified by Ashford & Lyle \u201cto the extent relevant to compliance costs\u201d. Exhibit E covers contract status, but the body does not require it.",
 "CFIUS uses the viability financials to monitor dependence on classified revenue (64.3% of FY2024 revenue). Limiting financial content to compliance costs does not meet NST 9.3(f).",
 "Add NST 9.3(d)\u2013(g) to \u00a7 12.3, and add organizational chart and viability-financials sections to Exhibit E.")
gap("9-D","No stub-period first report","Low",
 "NST 9.5: the first report covers the Closing Date through December 31 of the year of Closing.",
 "Not addressed.",
 "On a June 30, 2025 Closing, the first report (covering July 1 to December 31, 2025) is due March 31, 2026.",
 "Add NST 9.5.")

req_head(10, "Incident Reporting", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("10-A","72 hours from GSD determination rather than 24 hours from discovery","Critical",
 "NST 10.1: report within 24 hours of discovery. NST 10.2: \u201cdiscovery\u201d occurs when any Saxonbrook employee, officer, director, agent, contractor or representative first becomes aware of facts reasonably indicating a breach, and the obligation \u201cshall not be conditioned upon or delayed pending investigation, verification, or determination by the GSD.\u201d NST 10.4: the clock \u201ccommences upon discovery by any Saxonbrook personnel\u201d and does not depend on the GSD\u2019s awareness.",
 "\u00a7 14.2: within 72 hours after the GSD \u201cdetermines that a Reportable Incident has occurred.\u201d The GSD makes that determination \u201cas promptly as practicable\u201d, and the clock runs only from the GSD\u2019s \u201caffirmative determination.\u201d",
 "The draft triples the reporting window. It also makes the start of the clock open-ended and dependent on the GSD\u2019s determination, which is the gatekeeping step the NST forbids. All five precedents use 24 hours from discovery. Kit Holloway\u2019s view is that CFIUS has not, to our knowledge, accepted anything longer. Meridian\u2019s concern about unverified \u201cnoise\u201d is already answered by the NST: the initial report may be preliminary and limited to facts \u201cto the extent known\u201d, may be sent by e-mail (NST 10.3), and is followed by a detailed report. The obligation is therefore not \u201cduplicative\u201d; the NST itself requires it.",
 "Replace \u00a7 14.2 with NST 10.1\u201310.4: a preliminary written report (e-mail acceptable) to Dr. Keene within 24 hours of discovery by any Saxonbrook personnel, and a detailed follow-up within five business days. Jonathan\u2019s proposed 72-hour supplemental report may be added as an intermediate update, but it cannot replace the 24-hour notice and must not lengthen the five-business-day follow-up. Add an internal duty requiring all personnel to escalate immediately to the GSD, and cover it in training under \u00a7 16.1(e).")
gap("10-B","Follow-up report and contents","Medium",
 "NST 10.3: the initial report includes a preliminary description, the date and time of discovery and the persons involved. A detailed written follow-up is due within five business days.",
 "\u00a7 14.3 sets out a single, detailed report (contents (a)\u2013(g)). There is no two-stage structure.",
 "\u00a7 14.3\u2019s content list is good, but it should apply to the follow-up report.",
 "Two-stage structure: initial report (NST 10.3 contents) and follow-up report (the \u00a7 14.3 contents).")
gap("10-C","Parallel reporting incomplete; scope cross-check","Low",
 "NST 10.5: parallel reporting to DCSA, the cognizant security agency, the relevant contracting officer and other U.S. Government agencies. NST 10.1 covers any actual or suspected breach, including unauthorized access to Export-Controlled Technical Data or Classified Spaces.",
 "\u00a7 14.2: DCSA \u201cto the extent required by applicable NISPOM provisions\u201d. \u00a7 14.1(a) covers only classified information and facilities.",
 "Contracting officers and other agencies (e.g., DDTC voluntary disclosures) are not referenced. \u00a7 14.1(a) should also cover access to export-controlled data, although \u00a7 14.1(c)\u2013(d) catch most of it.",
 "Add NST 10.5, and extend \u00a7 14.1(a) to Export-Controlled Technical Data and Classified Spaces.")

req_head(11, "Government Contracts Continuity", "Non-compliant", "High")
gap("11-A","Notice period, recipient and triggers","High",
 "NST 11.2: 90 days\u2019 prior written notice delivered directly to the CFIUS monitoring contact of any decision to terminate, not rebid, or materially reduce the scope of a classified contract, with detailed reasons, impact and continuity steps.",
 "\u00a7 10.2: 60 days\u2019 notice to the Security Committee, which \u201cshall promptly inform CFIUS\u201d. The triggers are termination, non-renewal and non-rebid only.",
 "The draft shortens the period by 30 days and routes notice through an intermediary, so CFIUS could receive materially less than 60 days. Material reductions in scope are omitted. Four of five precedents use 90 days direct to CFIUS; only Precedent D used 60.",
 "Conform to NST 11.2: 90 days, direct to Dr. Keene, with a copy to the Security Committee, and include material scope reductions.")
gap("11-B","No CFIUS direction right during notice period","Medium",
 "NST 11.3: during the notice period, CFIUS may consult the contracting agencies and direct the steps necessary for continuity of supply and protection of classified information.",
 "None.",
 "The CFIUS direction right is omitted.",
 "Add NST 11.3.")
gap("11-C","No obligation to rebid or to consult before declining","High",
 "NST 11.4: commercially reasonable efforts to rebid and retain classified contracts. NST 11.5: Saxonbrook must consult CFIUS before declining to rebid.",
 "\u00a7 10.1 requires commercially reasonable efforts to continue performance of existing contracts. There is no rebid covenant and no consultation duty. Our matrix states that \u00a7 10.1 contains an \u201caffirmative obligation to pursue rebid\u201d; it does not.",
 "Both NST obligations are omitted. On the current timetable this matters: all three programs ($312.0M) will in time come up for recompetition.",
 "Add NST 11.4 and 11.5. Make clear that the \u201ccommercially unreasonable terms\u201d exception in NST 11.5 is available only after consultation with CFIUS.")
gap("11-D","Absolute maintenance covenant qualified","Low",
 "NST 11.1: maintain all existing classified contracts \u201cwithout interruption\u201d.",
 "\u00a7 10.1 states the covenant but adds \u201ccommercially reasonable efforts to continue performance\u201d.",
 "The efforts qualifier could be read to soften the unqualified maintenance obligation.",
 "Make the efforts language an additional obligation (\u201cand shall use\u201d), not a qualifier.")
gap("11-E","New-contract notification","Low",
 "NST App. A: prompt notice to CFIUS and DCSA of new classified awards, modifications, extensions or terminations.",
 "\u00a7 10.3: notice to the Security Committee and GSD within 30 days, and only where the award \u201cmaterially alter[s]\u201d security posture. \u00a7 13.1(e): \u201cprompt\u201d notice to CFIUS of new awards and material modifications (value change greater than 10%). DCSA is not covered.",
 "\u00a7\u00a7 10.3 and 13.1(e) are inconsistent with each other, and DCSA notice is omitted.",
 "Harmonize: prompt notice to CFIUS and DCSA of every new award, modification, extension or termination.")

req_head(12, "Subcontracting Restrictions", "Non-compliant", "High")
gap("12-A","25% direct-equity threshold rather than 10% direct or indirect","High",
 "NST 12.1: no subcontracting of classified work, without CFIUS\u2019s prior written approval, to any Meridian affiliate or any entity in which Meridian holds a 10% or greater interest, \u201cwhether such interest is held directly or indirectly, including through subsidiaries, affiliates, joint ventures, partnerships, or other arrangements.\u201d",
 "\u00a7 11.3: 25% or greater \u201cdirect equity interest\u201d, measured \u201cas reflected on Meridian\u2019s books and records.\u201d \u00a7 11.2: an absolute bar on Meridian and its subsidiaries, affiliates and parent. \u201cAffiliate\u201d is undefined.",
 "Greystone acknowledged that the 25% threshold was \u201cspecifically calibrated\u201d to exclude Meridian joint ventures in France, Germany, Japan and South Korea in which it holds 10\u201324% (Rees e-mail, Apr. 17). Those are the entities the NST is aimed at. The \u201cdirect\u201d qualifier excludes the joint-venture and consortium structures that NST 12.1 names. Measuring by Meridian\u2019s own books and records leaves Meridian to determine whether the test is met. All five precedents use 10%, and two expressly include indirect interests. The absolute bar in \u00a7 11.2 exceeds the NST and is acceptable, but because \u201caffiliate\u201d is undefined it cannot fill the gap.",
 "Conform to NST 12.1 (10%, direct or indirect). Answer the diligence-burden concern by requiring Meridian to deliver at signing, and update quarterly, a certified schedule of every entity in which it holds a direct or indirect interest of 10% or more. This puts the diligence burden on Meridian, which holds the information. Note that the NST requires prior CFIUS approval, not a ban. Approval requests for specific joint-venture subcontractors can be made case by case.")
gap("12-B","No lower-tier flow-down","High",
 "NST 12.2: the restriction applies at all tiers, and subcontractors must be contractually bound not to subcontract further to restricted entities without CFIUS approval.",
 "None.",
 "Without flow-down, classified work could reach a 10%-plus Meridian joint venture at the second tier.",
 "Add NST 12.2 and a mandatory flow-down clause.")
gap("12-C","\u201cClassified work\u201d undefined; list omits country of organization","Low",
 "NST 12.3 defines \u201cclassified work\u201d. NST 12.4: the subcontractor list includes country of organization and is available to CFIUS and the Monitor.",
 "No definition. \u00a7 11.4 lists name, address, ownership and work description, updated quarterly.",
 "These are minor conforming points. The quarterly update is stricter than the NST and acceptable.",
 "Add the NST 12.3 definition and country of organization.")

req_head(13, "Amendment and Termination", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("13-A","Amendments without CFIUS consent","Critical",
 "NST 13.1: amendment only with the prior written consent of all parties and CFIUS. No amendment, modification, waiver or supplement is effective unless signed by all parties and approved in writing by CFIUS. Waivers require CFIUS\u2019s express written consent.",
 "\u00a7 18.1: a written instrument signed by Saxonbrook, Meridian and the Voting Trustee. CFIUS is omitted, and so is Pinnacle, although it is a Party. \u00a7 18.9: a waiver is effective if signed \u201cby the Party granting such waiver\u201d.",
 "As drafted, the private parties could unilaterally amend or waive any mitigation term, including the voting trust. All precedents require CFIUS consent.",
 "Replace \u00a7 18.1 and \u00a7 18.9 with NST 13.1 word for word, covering all Parties and CFIUS.")
gap("13-B","Automatic termination with fixed 12-month wind-down","Critical",
 "NST 13.2: in force for the duration of Meridian\u2019s direct or indirect ownership, and does not lapse through the passage of time alone. NST 13.3: may survive divestiture at CFIUS\u2019s \u201csole and unreviewable discretion\u201d, including indefinitely. NST 13.4: termination only by petition to CFIUS, which may refuse or impose conditions.",
 "\u00a7 18.2: terminates \u201cautomatically upon the complete divestiture\u201d. Sections 8, 9, 12 and 14 survive for 12 months only, then \u201call obligations \u2026 shall cease.\u201d Ex. D \u00b6 II and Ex. B \u00b6 3 are tied to this mechanism.",
 "The fixed wind-down replaces CFIUS\u2019s discretion with a contractual end date. Divestiture to another foreign buyer, or a partial divestiture through indirect structures, could end the protections. \u201cOwnership interest\u201d is not stated to include indirect ownership. There is no petition mechanism. All precedents preserve CFIUS\u2019s discretion over survival.",
 "Replace \u00a7 18.2 with NST 13.2\u201313.4. Any wind-down period may be expressed only as a minimum survival period, subject to CFIUS\u2019s determination.")
gap("13-C","Evidence-preservation survival and other survival clauses","Low",
 "NST 13.3 (CFIUS determines survival).",
 "\u00a7 14.4: evidence is preserved for 5 years and survives termination.",
 "This is consistent with the NST and exceeds it. It should be preserved in the revised survival clause.",
 "Cross-reference in the revised \u00a7 18.2.")

req_head(14, "Penalties and Enforcement", "Non-compliant", "Critical")
gap("14-A","Penalty capped at $250,000; transaction-value measure omitted","Critical",
 "NST 14.1: civil penalties of up to $250,000 per violation or the value of the transaction, \u201cwhichever is greater\u201d. The transaction value is $588,285,000.",
 "\u00a7 17.1: penalties \u201cnot to exceed Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($250,000) per violation.\u201d",
 "The draft turns a minimum into a cap and removes an alternative measure of more than $588 million. CFIUS will not accept a contractual limit on its own penalty authority (NST 14.6\u201314.7). In addition, we understand that CFIUS\u2019s November 2024 amendments to its penalty regulations (31 C.F.R. \u00a7 800.901, effective December 2024) raised the per-violation maximum for breaches of mitigation agreements above the $250,000 figure stated in the NST. That should be confirmed before submission. Either way, a hard dollar cap in the Agreement is inadvisable.",
 "Track NST 14.1, and add \u201cor such greater amount as may be provided under 50 U.S.C. \u00a7 4565 and 31 C.F.R. Part 800 as in effect from time to time.\u201d")
gap("14-B","Continuing violations not treated as separate per-day violations","High",
 "NST 14.2: each day a violation continues is a separate violation.",
 "None.",
 "Read together with the 30-day cure period (Gap 14-D), the omission substantially reduces exposure for continuing breaches.",
 "Add NST 14.2.")
gap("14-C","Forced divestiture and Presidential authority omitted","Critical",
 "NST 14.4: potential forced divestiture under 50 U.S.C. \u00a7 4565(d)(4), with the parties\u2019 acknowledgment. NST 14.5: Presidential authority over classified contracts and FCLs. NST 14.6: remedies are cumulative.",
 "\u00a7 17.1 refers to injunctive relief and DOJ referral. \u00a7 17.3 preserves authority \u201cincluding \u2026 suspending or prohibiting the Transaction\u201d. Divestiture is not mentioned.",
 "Every precedent includes forced divestiture. Leaving out the parties\u2019 express acknowledgment will be read as deliberate.",
 "Insert NST 14.3\u201314.7 word for word, including Meridian\u2019s acknowledgment of the divestiture authority.")
gap("14-D","New 30-day cure period","High",
 "No cure period in the NST. Remedies are cumulative and CFIUS\u2019s authority \u201cis not limited, constrained, or waived\u201d (NST 14.6\u201314.7).",
 "\u00a7 17.2: 30 days to cure after CFIUS notice. Only a failure to cure \u201cshall constitute a material breach.\u201d",
 "The negative implication is that an uncured violation is not a material breach until 30 days have passed. That sits uneasily with per-violation penalties and per-day accrual, and limits CFIUS\u2019s remedies.",
 "Delete \u00a7 17.2. As a fallback, recast it as a discretionary cure that CFIUS may grant, stating expressly that it does not limit penalties, per-day accrual or any other remedy.")
EOF
echo ok'

doc.add_heading("Cross-Cutting Issues (Not Tied to a Single Requirement)", level=2)
gap("X-1","Wrong legal entity named on cover page, signature block and Exhibit E","High",
 "NST § II identifies the U.S. Business as Saxonbrook Precision Systems, Inc. (Delaware; EIN 63-4218907).",
 "The preamble and § 3.1 refer to Saxonbrook. The cover page, the signature block (“VANGUARD PRECISION SYSTEMS, INC.” over Ms. Harlow’s name) and the Exhibit E header name “Vanguard Precision Systems, Inc.”. The Saxonbrook notice e-mail uses the vanguardprecision.com domain.",
 "If executed in this form, the U.S. Business would not be a signatory under its correct name, which gives rise to an enforceability and FCL-identity problem that CFIUS and DCSA will notice. The NST acknowledgment block and the Security Profile title contain the same error.",
 "Confirm with Mr. Ostroff whether “Vanguard” is a former or trade name or a separate entity. Conform every reference to Saxonbrook Precision Systems, Inc. (adding an “f/k/a” or “d/b/a” only if accurate). Raise the NST acknowledgment-block error with Dr. Keene’s office.")
gap("X-2","No NST-precedence clause","Medium",
 "NST § V preamble: the NST controls in any ambiguity or conflict, and the Agreement may exceed but not “conflict with or diminish” the NST. NST § IV definitions are “incorporated into the Mitigation Agreement.”",
 "§ 2.3 deals only with conflicts with NISPOM and DCSA directives (“more restrictive provision shall control”). The definitions in § 1.1 depart from the NST definitions in several places (Foreign National; Classified Facilities instead of Classified Spaces; Board limited to Saxonbrook alone; U.S. Business without subsidiaries).",
 "Without a precedence clause, the departures would govern as between the private parties. CFIUS will insist on the clause in any event.",
 "Add: “In the event of any ambiguity or conflict between this Agreement and the NST, the NST shall control.” Adopt the NST § IV definitions, including “U.S. Business … together with its subsidiaries and controlled affiliates”, so that subsidiaries are covered.")
gap("X-3","Meridian-Nominated Directors who are U.S. citizens are not restricted","Medium",
 "NST 3.3(ii): the Foreign Acquirer may not receive non-public information about classified operations. NST 5.1: barriers between classified and export-controlled operations and Meridian.",
 "§ 4.2(b) and Ex. A bar only Meridian-Nominated Directors “who are Foreign Nationals” from classified access. There is no ITAR/EAR restriction. The Security Profile assumes all Meridian nominees will have no clearance and no access to classified or ITAR/EAR material.",
 "A U.S.-citizen Meridian nominee, acting as Meridian’s representative, could be a channel for information to Meridian even though he or she is not a Foreign National.",
 "Provide that all Meridian-Nominated Directors, whatever their citizenship, are excluded from Classified Information, Export-Controlled Technical Data, Classified Spaces and Security Committee matters, as the Security Profile assumes.")
gap("X-4","Effective Date / Closing / execution mechanics","Medium",
 "NST § VI: an executed agreement is to be submitted by May 3, 2025 (electronic, with hard copies by courier within five business days). Clearance is anticipated about May 15. No closing may occur before written clearance.",
 "Effective Date = CFIUS clearance (§ 1.1). Obligations are keyed variously to the Effective Date (§§ 2.2, 9.4) and to Closing (§§ 4.2, 5.1, 9.2). The cover page reads “DRAFT — NOT FOR EXECUTION”.",
 "The mixed triggers create the timing mismatches discussed in Gaps 5-E and 7-A. They also leave unclear which obligations apply between clearance and Closing.",
 "Key each obligation to the NST trigger (generally Closing). Add a no-closing-before-clearance covenant. Build the execution and submission logistics into the timetable (Part VI).")
gap("X-5","Undefined or inconsistent terms","Low",
 "NST § IV definitions.",
 "“Affiliate” (§§ 8.1, 11.2) and “sensitive but unclassified information” (§ 9.2(c)) are undefined. “Classified Facilities” is used in place of the NST’s “Classified Spaces”. The preamble cites 31 C.F.R. Part 802 (real estate transactions), which is not relevant.",
 "These are drafting-hygiene points.",
 "Define “Affiliate” to include any entity in which Meridian holds 10% or more, directly or indirectly (aligning with Requirement 12). Replace the undefined terms with the NST terms. Delete the Part 802 reference.")
gap("X-6","Inconsistent description of Dr. Kessler and the outgoing Board","Low",
 "NST § II: Dr. Kessler is a “current member of the board of directors.”",
 "Recitals and Ex. A ¶ V: “Founder and Director Emeritus”. The Security Profile describes him as Chairman of the Board. The post-Closing board in Ex. A omits Dr. Kessler and Mr. Ostroff without explanation.",
 "This factual inconsistency should be resolved before submission. Dr. Kessler’s post-Closing role is also a client-relations issue, given his 22% stake and his concerns about governance.",
 "Confirm the facts with Mr. Ostroff and conform the documents. Discuss Dr. Kessler’s post-Closing role with the client.")
EOF
echo ok'

doc.add_heading("V. Corrections to the April 17 Precedent Matrix and Related Work Product", level=1)
para("Before the precedent matrix is shared with Meridian’s counsel or relied on in a call with Treasury, the following entries should be corrected. In several places the matrix describes v3.2 as “consistent” with the NST when it is not. Relying on those entries would concede points we need to win.")
table(["Matrix row","Matrix says","Correct position"], [

# I. Bottom Line

Draft v3.2 is not in a form that can be submitted to CFIUS. Measured against the fourteen requirements in Section V of the National Security Terms ("NST"), not one requirement is fully satisfied without revision. We identify 71 discrete gaps: 12 Critical (each, in our judgment, likely on its own to cause CFIUS to reject the agreement or impose its own language), 26 High, 23 Medium and 10 Low. The NST is explicit that each requirement is a mandatory floor ("at a minimum"), that the parties may exceed but may not "conflict with or diminish" those requirements, and that the NST control in any conflict or ambiguity (NST § V, preamble). Several v3.2 provisions do exactly what that language forbids.

The submission deadline is May 3, 2025 (12 calendar days from today). The NST warns that failure to submit a satisfactory agreement may lead CFIUS to recommend that the President block or unwind the transaction (NST § I). Because v3.2 deviates on points where all five precedents in our matrix follow the NST, we do not believe the departures can be defended as market practice.

The issues that most need resolving before May 3, in priority order:

1.  **Board majority (Req. 1).** Three CFIUS-approved directors on a seven-member board is 42.9%, not a majority (NST 1.2). A nine-seat board (5 independents / 3 Meridian / 1 management, 55.6%, matching Precedent D) would let Meridian keep its "non-negotiable" three seats and still satisfy the NST.

2.  **Observer and consultation rights (Req. 3).** The consultation right (§ 6.1(c)) and Board Observer (§ 6.1(d)) are rights that NST 3.3 expressly prohibits by name ("consultation," "observer," attendance at Board meetings).

3.  **ITAR/EAR scope and the Foreign National definition (Req. 4).** Access restrictions cover only classified information and facilities.
